	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try.next && mv -f build/avra-try.next build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

# directory — the runtime's object and every std package — under
# lib/avra/. A program anywhere then says `use @std.io` with no
# manifest row, and links.
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
install: avra
	@mkdir -p $(PREFIX)/bin $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std

# std-avrac's cases that END THE SUITE'S PROCESS on the program layer, one a line, by the first line
# the runner says after `avra: while running `. Every case after one in its row never runs, so the
# gate fails on a trap this file does not list. Each has its place and the layer's words above it.
# Take a line away the day its case runs to an answer, then run its file: the cases past it report.
#
# features/annotations/tests/annotations_adversarial_test.av — `file_generated` (main.av) asked while it was being answered: program_refused -> file_erring -> law_findings -> file_generated -> fn_signature -> resolved -> generated_names (a same-file annotation fn whose answer names a type only a generator could declare)
features/annotations — the compile-time call's laws / the remaining seats and answer / a lookalike answer does not declare — only `Directive` does
#!/bin/sh
# Runs each spec directory's suite, stopping once the cases have reported.
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
cd /work/avra; unset AVRA_SPEC_DIFFERENTIAL
mkdir -p /tmp/runsK
for d in $(awk '{print $2}' /tmp/inv/dirs.txt); do
  n=$(echo $d | tr '/' '_')
  log=/tmp/runsK/$n.log
  [ -s "$log.done" ] && continue
  build/avra test packages/std-avrac/$d > $log 2>&1 &
  pid=$!
  while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do
    if grep -q 'tests passed\|^avra: while running' $log; then sleep 3; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; pkill -P $pid 2>/dev/null; break; fi
    sleep 5
  done
  wait $pid 2>/dev/null
  echo "$d $(grep -c '✗' $log) $(grep 'tests passed' $log) $(grep -c '^avra: while running' $log)" > $log.done
  cat $log.done
done
echo ALLDONE

/// A file `avra fix` stands over: the engine its program is asked through, the file, its text and
/// its package, and the file parsed whole. `edited` answers an engine over the program with the
/// file's text replaced, its world entered; `entered` enters the program's own world again.
export type FixOver = {
    engine: QueryEngine,
    h: ProgramFile,
    package: string,
    text: string,
    store: SyntaxArena,
    edited: fn(string) -> QueryEngine,
    entered: fn() -> void,
}

/// The file `h` of the program `engine` asks, in `package`, as `avra fix` stands over it.
export fn fix_over(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    h: ProgramFile,
    package: string,
    text: string,
    edited: fn(string) -> QueryEngine,
    entered: fn() -> void,
) -> FixOver {
    FixOver {
        engine: engine,
        h: h,
        package: package,
        text: text,
        store: fix_store(engine, h.file),
        edited: edited,
        entered: entered,
    }
}

impl FixOver {
    /// What the file says: its laws' diagnostics, then its rules', a rule's suggestions as its rewrites.
    fn diags() -> List<Diag> { file_law_diags(self.engine, self.h).concat(self.rule_diags()) }

    /// What the file's rules say, each suggestion as its rewrite.
    fn rule_diags() -> List<Diag> {
        [self.rewritten(said_diag(k, self.h.full)) for k in file_rule_rows(self.engine, self.package, self.h.file).said]
    }

    /// A rule's diagnostic, each edit of its suggestions as `avra fix` splices a rule's rewrite.
    fn rewritten(d: Diag) -> Diag {
        d with { suggestions: [sg with { edits: [rule_rewrite(self.text, e) for e in sg.edits] } for sg in d.suggestions] }
    }

    /// Each suggestion of `diags` fix considers, proved or accepted by its rule's law, or only shown.
    fn proved(diags: List<Diag>) -> List<Application> {
        let before = file_code(self.engine, self.h.file)
        flatten(
            [[self.proved_one(before, d.kind, sg) for sg in d.suggestions if fix_considers(self.store, sg)] for d in diags],
        )
    }

    fn proved_one(before: FileCode?, kind: string, sg: Suggestion) -> Application {
        let provable = edits_provable(self.engine, self.h.file, sg.edits)
        let after = self.after(sg.edits)
        let proved = provable && after != null && same_code(before, file_code(after!, self.h.file))
        let law = rule_law(kind)
        let by_law = if proved || law == null || after == null { null } else { if program_erring(after!, self.package).is_empty() { law } else { null } }
        (self.entered)()
        Application { kind: kind, edits: sg.edits, proved: proved, by_law: by_law }
    }

    /// Each certain suggestion of an error among `diags`, accepted where it clears the error.
    fn repairs(diags: List<Diag>) -> List<Application> {
        let was = fix_errors(diags)
        flatten(
            [[Application {
                kind: d.kind,
                edits: sg.edits,
                proved: false,
                by_law: null,
                repaired: self.clears(was, sg.edits),
            } for sg in d.suggestions if fix_repairs(self.store, sg)] for d in diags if is_error(d)],
        )
    }

    /// Whether `edits` leave the program erring nowhere, or its file with fewer of the errors `was`
    /// lists and none it didn't.
    fn clears(was: List<string>, edits: List<Edit>) -> bool {
        let after? = self.after(edits) else { return false }
        let now = fix_errors(file_law_diags(after, self.h))
        let clear = program_erring(after, self.package).is_empty()
        (self.entered)()
        if clear { return true }
        now.length < was.length && now.all((e) -> was.contains(e))
    }

    /// An engine over the program with `edits` spliced into the file; absent where one reaches
    /// outside the file or two overlap.
    fn after(edits: List<Edit>) -> QueryEngine? {
        if edits.is_empty() || edits.any(it.loc.file != null && it.loc.file! != self.h.full) { return null }
        let text? = spliced(self.text, edits) else { return null }
        (self.edited)(text)
    }
}

fn suggestion_apps_of(main: string, d: Diag, only: string? = null) -> List<Application> {
    fixing(main).proved(of_kind([d], only))
}

// LICENSED nullable.repeated_unwrap: `x!` inside these fixture strings is idiom text under

fn fix_apps_of(main: string, only: string? = null) -> List<Application> {
    let fx = fixing(main)
    fx.proved(of_kind(fx.rule_diags(), only))
}

/// The repairs `avra fix --repair` makes of a program that has errors, never the proved tier.
fn repair_apps_of(main: string, only: string? = null) -> List<Application> {
    let fx = fixing(main)
    fx.repairs(of_kind(fx.law_diags(), only))
}

/// Whether the program whose one file is `text` builds refused nothing.
fn checks_clean(text: string) -> bool { fix_held(text).judged_at(FIX_PATH).clean() }

//! The formatter's idioms for this feature — `rule`s, reached by
//! this feature's `mod.av`, the way any declaration is.
use core.{StmtId, ExprId, SyntaxArena}
use features.{Code, Fix, fact_rule}

/// An `impl Trait for T` method whose body is the trait's own
/// DEFAULT body for that name, span-blind and with a written no-op
/// (`nothing()`) elided on either side, is a copy: omitting it
/// inherits the identical default (`Decls.defaulted`), so the
/// override says nothing the trait does not already say.

/// The code the file `file` lowers to, read whole: each fn's, each method's and static's an impl
/// writes, and the statements it runs, each with the lambdas it lifts, in the order written; absent
/// where a body doesn't lower whole, which proves nothing.
export fn file_code(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> FileCode? {
    mut out: List<List<Ins>> = []
    for d in file_declares(engine, file).names {
        if d.kind is .Fn {
            let l? = lowered_fn(engine, file, d.name) else { return null }
            if !l.missing.is_empty() { return null }
            out = out.concat(renamed_bodies(l))
        }
    }
    for at in 0..item_count(engine, file) {
        let item = read_item(engine, file, at)
        for a in impls_at(engine, file, at) {
            for s in impl_fns(item, a) {
                let p? = item.store.fn_parts(s) else { continue }
                let l? = lowered_method(engine, a, p.name, item.store.is_static(s)) else { return null }
                if !l.missing.is_empty() { return null }
                out = out.concat(renamed_bodies(l))
            }
        }
    }
    let entry = lowered_entry(engine, file)
    if entry != null { out = out.concat(renamed_bodies(entry!)) }
    FileCode { bodies: out }
}

/// A lowered body and each lambda it lifts, its registers renamed.
fn renamed_bodies(l: LoweredFn) -> List<List<Ins>> {
    [alpha_renamed(l.ins, l.params.length)]
        .concat([alpha_renamed(f.ins, f.params.length) for f in l.lifts])
}

/// Whether two files' code is the same, body for body; a file that doesn't lower whole is no code.

    let x? = a else { return false }
    let y? = b else { return false }
    x.bodies.length == y.bodies.length &&
        [i for i in 0..x.bodies.length if !same_ins_list(x.bodies[i], y.bodies[i])].is_empty()
}

fn unused_imports(engine: QueryEngine, program: string, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem) -> List<
    UnusedImport,
> {
    let lines = [s for s in item.stmts if item.store.use_parts(s) != null && !item.store.is_exported(s)]
    if lines.is_empty() { return [] }
    let used = read_set(engine, program)
    [UnusedImport { stmt: s, names: names } for s in lines for names in [unread_names(engine, file, item.store.use_parts(s)!, used)] if !names.is_empty()]
}

/// The names one `use` line imports whose declarations `used` holds none of.

> {
    [name for j, name in u.items if !import_read(engine, file, local_name(u, j), used)]

fn read_set(engine: QueryEngine, package: string) -> Map<string, bool> {
    let keys = program_reads(engine, package).keys
    let said = keys.join("\\n")

    set
}

/// A program's reads, spelled one a line, and the same as a set.
type KeptReads = { said: string, set: Map<string, bool> }

/// Each program's reads as a set, by its package, once a process: a package another program of
/// that name reads otherwise is made again.
once fn read_sets() -> Cell<Map<string, KeptReads>> {
    let none: Map<string, KeptReads> = {}
    Cell.new(none)
}

The `references_test` port is on the layer and bundled, and I dropped my `rule_fix`/`rule_proof` work so the defects lane's version is the only one. I'm waiting on two answers from the lead before starting anything new.

**What changed on the branch.** I took out my earlier commit with the `rule_fix_test` and `rule_proof_test` ports, the declared-names fix to the proof, and the shared fix door. I kept a copy locally at tag `keep/fixover-8436fb02` in case their port has no shared door. The branch is now the base55 merge plus one new commit (69810d50), bundled as `base55..HEAD` in `/work/avra-lane-spec-harness.bundle`.

**`references_test` on the layer.** It now asks the same `Code` facts a fact rule asks, through the per-item input the layer already builds for its rules (`item_rule_file`, exposed to specs as `Judged.rule_files`). 21 cases run with 0 failures, then the file stops at a trap I listed. 4 cases after that trap never run. I moved that spec to the end of the file so the template cases still run.

**Compiler bug fixed.** `read_set` in `compiler/item_rules.av` cached a program's reads once per process, keyed only by package name. A second program with the same package name in one process got the first program's answer, so the same case passed or failed depending on test order. It now reuses the cache only while the reads are the same. A single CLI run never hit this; the spec harness and any long-running process do.

**Two traps on the layer, both added to `tools/gate/std-avrac.traps`.**
- `Code.callers()` stops the process on the layer ("unwrapped an absent value"), so any fact rule that calls it would kill a layer check. Its 3 cases are in a new file, `references_callers_test.av`, so the trap stops only that file.
- An annotation fn declared in a sibling file sends `fn_signature` into a loop. This is the same family as the trap already listed for a same-file annotation fn.

The std-avrac idioms check is clean and the changed files are formatted. Notes are in `/work/avra-lane-spec-harness.md` and the updated file list is `/work/avra-lane-spec-harness.tsv`.

**Waiting on the lead:**
- **`read_set_test`:** most of its 29 cases test a hoist/tree/direct decision that only the old lowering makes. I need to know whether those cases are marked old-path-only or pinned as layer gaps.

fn expr_name(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> ReadName? {
    match store.expr(e).use_shape() {
        .Read -> value_read(store.ident_name(e)),
        .Callee -> value_read(store.call_parts(e)?.callee),
        .Method(_, _) -> null,
        .Record(name) -> type_read(name.of),
        .Component(word) -> type_read(word),
        .TypeName(name) -> type_read(name),
    }
}

/// A type's name read.
fn type_read(name: string) -> ReadName { ReadName { space: Space.Type, name: name } }

fn value_read(name: string?) -> ReadName? {
    let n? = name else { return null }
    value_named(n)
}

/// A value's name read.
fn value_named(name: string) -> ReadName { ReadName { space: Space.Value, name: name } }

--- content ---
// The read set: which `state` places a body reads and a fn reaches,
// asked of the program layer. A closure is a boundary (its captures
// are the read, never its body), a call is a boundary (the callee's
// reads are another body's, folded in through any cycle), and a body
// reading nothing reads nothing. A place is a module `state`'s key, or
// `?` for one no caller can name (a body's own `state`).
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Judged}

const READ_PATH: string = "/w/src/main.av"

/// The program `source` writes, judged on the layer.
fn read_judged(source: string) -> Judged {
    held_at(
        {"/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n", READ_PATH: source},
        "/w",
    )
        .judged_at(READ_PATH)
}

/// What the fn `name` reads of the program's state by its own body.
fn reads(source: string, name: string) -> List<string> { read_judged(source).state_reads_of(READ_PATH, name) }

/// What the fn `name` reaches, by its body and every fn it calls.
fn reaches(source: string, name: string) -> List<string> { read_judged(source).state_reaches_of(READ_PATH, name) }

/// Whether `places` is the one module `state` named `name`.
fn only_state(places: List<string>, name: string) -> bool { places.length == 1 && places[0].ends_with("\t${name}") }

spec "features/read_set" {
    given "a body reading one state directly" {
        then "the read set holds exactly that place" { reads("fn f() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n + 1\n}", "f").length == 1 }
    }
    given "a body reading no state" {
        then "the read set is empty" { reads("fn f() -> int { 1 + 2 }", "f").is_empty() }
    }
    given "a subtree reading a parameter" {
        then "it reads no state" { reads("fn f(x: int) -> int { x + 1 }", "f").is_empty() }
    }
    given "a subtree reading an outer local" {
        then "the local is no state" { reads("fn f(x: int) -> int {\n    let y = x\n    y + 1\n}", "f").is_empty() }
    }
    given "a leaf reading a state place and a parameter" {
        then "the read set holds the one place" { reads("fn f(x: int) -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n + x\n}", "f").length == 1 }
    }
    given "a closure capturing a state place" {
        then "the capture is the read" { reads("fn f() -> fn() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    () -> n + 1\n}", "f").length == 1 }
        then "a state the closure BINDS itself is not the body's read" {
            reads("fn f() -> fn() -> int {\n    () -> {\n        state m: int = 0\n        m + 1\n    }\n}", "f").is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "a body calling a fn whose body reads no state" {
        then "the callee reaches nothing" { reaches("fn g() -> int { 1 }\nfn f() -> int { g() + 1 }", "g").is_empty() }
    }
    given "a body calling a fn that reads state" {
        then "the callee reaches it" {
            !reaches("fn g() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n\n}\nfn f() -> int { g() + 1 }", "g").is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "a call that chains two declarations deep to a state read" {
        then "the answer is TRANSITIVE" {
            let source = "fn h() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n\n}\nfn g() -> int { h() }\nfn f() -> int { g() }"
            !reaches(source, "h").is_empty() && !reaches(source, "g").is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "mutual recursion with no state read" {
        then "the fixpoint settles: the cycle is pure" { reaches("fn a() -> int { b() }\nfn b() -> int { a() }", "a").is_empty() }
    }
    given "mutual recursion that reaches a state read" {
        then "the cycle is impure" {
            !reaches("fn a() -> int { b() }\nfn b() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    a() + n\n}", "a").is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "a body reading two state places" {
        then "the read set holds both" {
            reads("fn f() -> int {\n    state x: int = 1\n    state y: int = 2\n    x + y\n}", "f").length == 2
        }
    }
    given "a top-level state place" {
        then "a body reading it reads that declaration" { only_state(reaches("state n: int = 0\nfn f() -> int { n + 1 }", "f"), "n") }
        then "a body reading two of them reads both" {
            reaches("state x: int = 1\nstate y: int = 2\nfn f() -> int { x + y }", "f").length == 2
        }
        then "a call to a fn reading exactly one reaches that place, through the callee" {
            let source = "state n: int = 0\nfn g() -> int { n }\nfn f() -> int { g() + 1 }"
            only_state(reaches(source, "f"), "n") && !reaches(source, "g").is_empty()
        }
        then "a call chain two deep carries the place all the way" {
            only_state(reaches("state n: int = 0\nfn h() -> int { n }\nfn g() -> int { h() }\nfn f() -> int { g() }", "f"), "n")
        }
        then "calls to fns reading two different ones reach both" {
            reaches(
                "state x: int = 1\nstate y: int = 2\nfn gx() -> int { x }\nfn gy() -> int { y }\nfn f() -> int { gx() + gy() }",
                "f",
            )
                .length == 2
        }
        then "a cycle reaching a place carries it through every member" {
            let source = "state n: int = 0\nfn a() -> int { b() }\nfn b() -> int { a() + n }"
            let pa = reaches(source, "a")
            let pb = reaches(source, "b")
            only_state(pa, "n") && only_state(pb, "n")
        }
    }
    given "a callee's own local state" {
        then "is a place a caller cannot name" {
            let reached = reaches("fn g() -> int {\n    state m: int = 0\n    m\n}\nfn f() -> int { g() + 1 }", "g")
            reached.length == 1 && reached[0] == "?"
        }
    }
    given "a declaration's places" {
        then "are none for a pure fn, and once each for a reader" {
            let source = "state x: int = 1\nstate y: int = 2\nfn p() -> int { 1 }\nfn r() -> int { y + x + y }"
            reaches(source, "p").is_empty() && reaches(source, "r").length == 2
        }
    }
}

layer: a generator reads its own signature among written names alone

Generating a module's declarations runs its annotation fns, and running one read the fn's
signature through `fn_signature`, whose types resolve through what the module's generators make.

signature can't depend on what generators make, so `generator_signature` (item_signatures.av)

(handed_args, annotation_kind, validates, judges) asks it; a program's typing still reads

  a fn's reach (pure callee, impure callee, transitive ×2, mutual pure, mutual impure, a top-level state read directly / two of them /
  through a callee / two deep / two callees / through a cycle, a callee's local = `?`, a pure fn none + a reader once each).
- features/tests/read_set_workspace_test.av — INTERNAL (old path, 29/29), for the deletion map. The mechanism parts it asserts, none with a layer counterpart:
  `site_lowering` DIRECT (local + global ×3), `hoistable`/Hoist (no state, own local, pure callee, closure arg, mutual pure), Tree

waiting on your go/no-go for the "absent source said in words" law before porting input_host_test; the port's shape depends on it. Case split I'll use:
INTERNAL (old Host/Workspace mechanism): spared_text/Beneath/InputName digest cases ×9, ws.source on a live workspace ×5, after_program ×2.
Ported to the layer (behaviour): an empty file is an empty program; missing / not-text / refused / dangling are said in words, each distinct (needs the law); and a re-check after an edit, truncation, removal or unreadable file names the file's current line or says why, run through a second engine over the same store ×6.
</to_controller>

`input_host_test` is on hold until the lead answers one question; the port's shape depends on it.

**The finding.** On the program layer, a file in `src/` that isn't valid UTF-8, or that is a link pointing nowhere, is silently skipped: `avra check` exits 0 and says nothing. The old path refuses both in words ("`…/bin.av` is not UTF-8 — byte 0", "`…/dangle.av` does not exist") and exits 2. An empty file behaves the same on both paths. The cause is that the layer's file-text input only answers "text, or nothing", so the reason is lost. The layer's file-octets input already knows the reason (missing, a link, refused, or bytes that aren't text).

**Decision needed from the lead:** may I add a layer law that, for every listed source file with no text, says why from the octets read, in the old path's words? It would get the same kind of witness as the traps: red now, green after, agreeing with the old path.

**Planned split of the 22 cases:**

| Kind | Cases | How |
|---|---|---|
| Old-path mechanism, kept as old-path-only (INTERNAL) | 9 host-read and digest cases, 5 reads through a long-lived workspace, 2 "after-program" overlay cases | kept for the deletion map |
| Ported, needs the law | missing, not-text, refused and dangling files each said in words, each distinct | waits on the answer |
| Ported, independent of the law | an empty file is an empty program | ready to write |
| Ported, independent except the removed and unreadable ones | a re-check after an edit, a truncation, a removal or the file turning unreadable names the file's current line or says why (6 cases, a second engine over the same store) | the edit and truncation cases are ready to write |

/// A fault as a finding keeps it: its name, the literal, where it was read from, and what it says.
fn fault_words(fault: EmbedFault, rel: string, base: EmbedBase) -> List<string> {
    let from = if base is .Beside { BESIDE } else { ROOT }
    match fault {
        .Outside -> ["outside", rel, from, ""],
        .Undeclared(key) -> ["undeclared", rel, from, key],
        .Linked -> ["linked", rel, from, ""],
        .Missing -> ["missing", rel, from, ""],
        .NotText(at) -> ["not_text", rel, from, "${at}"],
        .Refused(why) -> ["refused", rel, from, why],
    }
}

/// A fault from the words a finding keeps.
fn kept_fault(a: List<string>) -> EmbedFault {
    match a[0] {
        "outside" -> EmbedFault.Outside,
        "undeclared" -> EmbedFault.Undeclared(a[3]),
        "linked" -> EmbedFault.Linked,
        "missing" -> EmbedFault.Missing,
        "not_text" -> EmbedFault.NotText(parse_int(a[3]) ?? 0),
        _ -> EmbedFault.Refused(a[3]),
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every kind a voice speaks by literal is a REGISTERED kind.

`refusal`, `warning` and `error_at` take the kind as their first
argument; a literal there that docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md (generated from the
assembled registry by `make witnesses`) has no entry for is a voice that
speaks a kind nothing registered — no row, no summary, no witness, no
help for `avra docs` to find. Reports what it examined."""
import re, sys
import avsrc

CALL = re.compile(r'\b(?:refusal|warning|error_at)\(\s*"([a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+)"')
# The CLI's own failure wrapper is a kind of the program `avra`, never of
# the language the registry describes.
OUTSIDE = {"build.command_failed"}
registered = set(re.findall(r'^## (\S+)$', open('docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md').read(), re.M))
if not registered:
    print("voices-spoken: docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md names no kind — nothing to compare against")
    sys.exit(1)
spoken = {}
files = avsrc.av_files(['packages/*/src'])
for f in files:
    text = open(f).read()
    for m in CALL.finditer(text):
        spoken.setdefault(m.group(1), (f, text[:m.start()].count('\n') + 1))
missing = sorted(k for k in spoken if k not in registered and k not in OUTSIDE)
for k in missing:
    f, line = spoken[k]
    print(f"voices-spoken: `{k}` is spoken at {f}:{line} and no registry row names it")
print(f"voices-spoken: {len(spoken)} spoken kind(s) in {len(files)} file(s) held against {len(registered)} registered")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)

def in_test_file(said):
    """Whether the first error `said` stands in a test file — one a build never reads unless its
    entry reaches it, and `check` judges: the program layer is judged by `check` there."""
    lines = said.splitlines()
    at = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if ERROR.match(l)), None)
    if at is None:
        return False
    place = next((l for l in lines[at + 1:at + 3] if "╭─[" in l), "")
    path = place.split("╭─[", 1)[-1].rsplit("]", 1)[0].split(":", 1)[0]
    return path.endswith("_test.av") or "/tests/" in path


def judged(avra, scratch, w):
    """One witness's row: its code, its verdict, its owner, and both first lines."""
    code = w["code"]
    row = {"code": code, "owner": owner(code), "old": "", "new": ""}
    if w["shape"] in ("beyond", "absent"):
        return dict(row, verdict=w["shape"].upper(), old=w["why"])
    if any(p.startswith("/std/") for p in w["files"]):
        return dict(row, verdict="STD-ROOT")
    case = os.path.join(scratch, "cases", re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", code))
    pkg = laid_out(case, w["files"])
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET", None)
    # the old path by name: since the flip the program layer is the default
    env["AVRA_PROGRAM"] = "0"
    env["AVRA_CACHE_DIR"] = os.path.join(case, "machine")
    # a witness using a form only the program layer builds is never asked of the old path
    forms = new_only(avra, pkg, dict(env, AVRA_PROGRAM="1", PWD=pkg))
    if forms:
        shutil.rmtree(case, ignore_errors=True)
        return dict(row, verdict="NEW-ONLY", new=forms[0])
    old_verb = "build" if w["shape"] == "built" else "check"
    old_exit, old_said = run([avra, old_verb, pkg], pkg, dict(env, PWD=pkg))

// A source as the program layer reads it: what a file that is there,
// empty, missing, not text, refused or a link to nothing makes of a
// program — each said in its own words, never one silence — and what a
// check over the same store says once the file has moved under it.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Held, Judged}
use @std.avrac.testing.held.{empty_store}
use @std.program.source_facts.{FileOctets}

const HOST_MAIN: string = "/w/src/main.av"

const HOST_OTHER: string = "/w/src/other.av"

/// The package whose entry is `main` and whose other source is `other`.
fn host_held(main: string, other: string) -> Held {
    held_at(
        {"/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n", HOST_MAIN: main, HOST_OTHER: other},
        "/w",
    )
}

/// The package whose other source holds no text, as a read of its octets finds `octets`.
fn unread_held(octets: FileOctets) -> Held { host_held("1\n", "") with { unread: {HOST_OTHER: octets} } }

/// The kinds a judged program says, in order.
fn kinds_said(j: Judged) -> List<string> { [d.kind for d in j.diagnostics] }

/// The message of the one diagnostic of `kind` a judged program says, empty for none.
fn said_of(j: Judged, kind: string) -> string { j.diagnostics.find(it.kind == kind)?.message ?? "" }

/// The source line the unwritten-`mut` rule names in the other source, judged over `store`.
fn mut_line(h: Held, store: StoreInMemory) -> string? {
    h.judged_over(HOST_MAIN, store).findings().find(it.rule == "let_stmt.unmutated_mut")?.text
}

spec "compiler/input_host — a source as the program layer reads it" {
    given "nothing there" {
        then "an empty source is there, and empty: the program says nothing of it" {
            host_held("1\n", "").judged_at(HOST_MAIN).diagnostics.is_empty()
        }
        then "a missing source is said in words, by its path" {
            let j = unread_held(FileOctets.Missing).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)
            kinds_said(j).join(",") == "source.missing" && said_of(j, "source.missing").contains(HOST_OTHER)
        }
        then "a missing source and an empty one say apart" {
            !host_held("1\n", "").judged_at(HOST_MAIN).diagnostics.any(it.kind == "source.missing") &&
                unread_held(FileOctets.Missing).judged_at(HOST_MAIN).diagnostics.any(it.kind == "source.missing")
        }
    }
    given "a source the host will not give as text" {
        then "octets that are no text are said by kind, from the byte that isn't" {
            let j = unread_held(FileOctets.Read([97, 255].bytes()!)).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)
            kinds_said(j).join(",") == "source.not_text" && said_of(j, "source.not_text").contains("byte 1")
        }
        then "a refusal is said by kind, in the host's own words" {
            let one = unread_held(FileOctets.Refused("permission denied (os error 13)")).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)
            let other = unread_held(FileOctets.Refused("EACCES")).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)
            kinds_said(one).join(",") == "source.refused" &&
                kinds_said(other).join(",") == "source.refused" &&
                said_of(one, "source.refused").contains("os error 13")
        }
        then "a refused source and a missing one say apart" {
            kinds_said(unread_held(FileOctets.Refused("x")).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)).join(",") !=
                kinds_said(unread_held(FileOctets.Missing).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)).join(",")
        }
        then "a link to nothing is said as one" {
            kinds_said(unread_held(FileOctets.Linked).judged_at(HOST_MAIN)).join(",") == "source.dangling"
        }
    }
    given "a source that is there" {
        then "its text is what the host holds" {
            host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n").judged_at(HOST_MAIN).findings().find(it.rule == "let_stmt.unmutated_mut")?.text == "mut a = 0"
        }
    }
    given "a check over a store an earlier check left, once the source moved" {
        then "an unchanged source names the line it holds" {
            let store = empty_store()
            let h = host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n")
            let _ = mut_line(h, store)
            mut_line(h, store) == "mut a = 0"
        }
        then "an edited source names its current line" {
            let store = empty_store()
            let _ = mut_line(host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n"), store)
            mut_line(host_held("1\n", "mut b = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { b }\n"), store) == "mut b = 0"
        }
        then "a source truncated to empty names no line — never the old one" {
            let store = empty_store()
            let _ = mut_line(host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n"), store)
            mut_line(host_held("1\n", ""), store) == null
        }
        then "a source that is gone is said as missing — never analysed as empty in silence" {
            let store = empty_store()
            let h = host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n")
            let _ = mut_line(h, store)
            let gone = h with { unread: {HOST_OTHER: FileOctets.Missing} }
            kinds_said(gone.judged_over(HOST_MAIN, store)).contains("source.missing")
        }
        then "a source that turned unreadable is said as not text" {
            let store = empty_store()
            let h = host_held("1\n", "mut a = 0\nexport fn f() -> int { a }\n")
            let _ = mut_line(h, store)
            let turned = h with { unread: {HOST_OTHER: FileOctets.Read([255].bytes()!)} }
            kinds_said(turned.judged_over(HOST_MAIN, store)).contains("source.not_text")
        }
    }
}

/// The name the package at `root` is addressed by: its manifest's, else, a directory with none, the
/// directory's own.
fn package_named(root: string) -> string { on_disk().package_named(root, file_name(root)) }

/// A file a build reads as data: its octets beneath its package's root, reached through no link.
fn disk_octets(root: string, path: string) -> FileOctets {
    match disk_beneath(root, path, EmbedKind.Octets) {
        .Octets(octets) -> FileOctets.Read(octets),
        .Text(text) -> FileOctets.Read(text.bytes()),
        .Missing -> FileOctets.Missing,
        .Linked -> FileOctets.Linked,
        .NotText(_) -> FileOctets.Refused("not text"),
        .Refused(why) -> FileOctets.Refused(why),
    }
}

/// directory names, or anything at all, stands behind the failure.
fn unopened(e: IoError, path: string) -> Beneath {
    match e {
        .NotFound(_) -> Beneath.Missing,
        .Denied(_) or .Holed(_, _) or .NotText(_, _) -> Beneath.Refused(e.describe().message),
        .IsDirectory(_) or .NotDirectory(_) or .Failed(_, _) -> if exists(path) || named_in_dir(path) { Beneath.Linked } else { Beneath.Refused(e.describe().message) },
    }
}

/// Whether the directory `path` stands in names it: a link to nothing is named where nothing
/// stands.
fn named_in_dir(path: string) -> bool {
    match list_dir(dir_of(path)) { .Ok(names) -> names.contains(file_name(path)), .Err(_) -> false }
}''')

A source file the program layer can't read as text is now refused by its cause, and `input_host_test` is split and on the layer. The bundle is refreshed (`base55..HEAD`, a06c5cdd).

**The new check.** Before this change, a file in `src/` that was missing, not valid UTF-8, refused by the OS, or a link pointing nowhere was skipped. `avra check` said nothing and exited 0. Now each cause is its own case in an enum and has its own diagnostic kind: `source.missing`, `source.not_text`, `source.refused`, `source.dangling`. Each comes with help text, a golden entry in `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md`, and a `make voices` witness. `make voices` reports no gaps for these four kinds.

The witness system couldn't express "a file with no text", so I added a witness shape for it (`Witness.Unread`). It is judged on the program layer, because the old path stops the run on these files instead of reporting a diagnostic kind.

**Before and after on a real directory:**

| File in `src/` | Before | Now | Old path |
|---|---|---|---|
| not valid UTF-8 | silent, exit 0 | `error[source.not_text]` "… is not UTF-8 — byte 0" | same words, but ends the run |
| link pointing nowhere | silent, exit 0 | `error[source.dangling]` | "does not exist", ends the run |

**A related CLI change.** The disk reader used to report a link pointing nowhere as "refused by the host". It now reports it as a link, which also affects `embed`. The embed suites still pass (std-avrac 22/22, CLI 10/10).

**`input_host_test` split:**
- **Layer file (13/13):** the four causes said apart, and an empty file as an empty program. It also covers a re-check over the same store after the file was edited, truncated, removed or made unreadable.
- **Old-path file, kept as old-path-only (22/22):** the old host's own reads, digests, long-lived workspace and "after-program" cases, kept for the deletion map.

Idioms show nothing new in std-avrac or cli.

**Problems already in base55, not caused by this change:**
- `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md` was out of date at base55; the compiler from before my changes shows the same differences. I regenerated it from the tree.
- `make voices` fails at base55 on 7 kinds that have no witness: `type.component_default`, `type.slot_shadows`, and five `ctx.*` kinds. I've asked the lead whose they are.

Next is `error_sites_test` (18 cases).

//! raises, and through each `?` site whose call answers another `_` fn's `Result`, whatever that
//! fn raises, through any recursion, each strongly connected set of such fns folded once. A body's

//! what a fn raises never asks what another raises to type a body: the sites are one question per

/// The shapes as a package, analyzed: the consumes pass is read off the
/// workspace's own table, never off a one-shot analysis's lowering, whose
/// workspace is disarmed before it lowers.
fn shaped() -> Workspace {
    let ws = test_workspace(
        memory_host(
            {
                "/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n",
                "/w/src/main.av": shapes,
            },
            ["/w/avra.toml", "/w/src/main.av"],
        ),
        "/w",
    )
    let _ = ws.analyze_file("/w/src/main.av")
    ws
}

/// Whether the one fn named `name` consumes its seat `j`.
fn consumes(ws: Workspace, name: string, j: int) -> bool {
    let fns = [x.id for x in ws.decls.all_decls() if x.name == name]
    fns.length == 1 && ws.decls.consumed_seat(fns[0], j)
}

/// Whether the one fn named `name` exists and borrows its seat `j`.
fn borrows(ws: Workspace, name: string, j: int) -> bool {
    let fns = [x.id for x in ws.decls.all_decls() if x.name == name]
    fns.length == 1 && !ws.decls.consumed_seat(fns[0], j)
}

// The interprocedural read set, asked of the program layer: whether a fn
// reaches `state` through any call, in any file of its package, through
// any cycle — a fixpoint over the declarations' call graph.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Judged}

/// The package whose files `files` lay beside its manifest, judged at `/w/src/main.av` or, where
/// it writes none, its first file.
fn pure_judged(files: Map<string, string>) -> Judged {
    mut all = files
    all.set("/w/avra.toml", "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")
    held_at(all, "/w").judged_at(files.keys()[0])
}

/// Whether the fn `name` the file at `path` declares reaches any state.
fn reaches_state(j: Judged, path: string, name: string) -> bool { !j.state_reaches_of(path, name).is_empty() }

const PURE_MAIN: string = "/w/src/main.av"

spec "compiler/pure_decl — the read-reach fixpoint is transitive" {
    given "a fn reading state, a caller of it, and a pure fn" {
        then "the caller's answer chains to the callee's" {
            let j = pure_judged({PURE_MAIN: "fn h() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n\n}\nfn g() -> int { h() }\nfn p() -> int { 1 }\n"})
            reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "h") && reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "g") && !reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "p")
        }
    }
    given "mutual recursion" {
        then "the fixpoint settles: a cycle with no state read is pure" {
            let j = pure_judged({PURE_MAIN: "fn a() -> int { b() }\nfn b() -> int { a() }\n"})
            !reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "a") && !reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "b")
        }
        then "a cycle that reaches a state read is impure" {
            let j = pure_judged(
                {PURE_MAIN: "fn a() -> int { b() }\nfn b() -> int { c() }\nfn c() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    a() + n\n}\n"},
            )
            reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "a") && reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "b") && reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "c")
        }
    }
    given "an `extern` fn has no body here" {
        then "it MAY read state — never pure" {
            reaches_state(pure_judged({PURE_MAIN: "extern fn c_read() -> int\nfn f() -> int { c_read() }\n"}), PURE_MAIN, "f")
        }
    }
    given "a callee in ANOTHER file of the package" {
        then "a pure callee folds: the caller is pure" {
            let j = pure_judged({"/w/src/a.av": "fn mk(n: int) -> int { n + 1 }\n", "/w/src/b.av": "fn f() -> int { mk(1) }\n"})
            !reaches_state(j, "/w/src/b.av", "f")
        }
        then "a state-reading callee folds: the caller reads state" {
            let j = pure_judged(
                {"/w/src/a.av": "fn g() -> int {\n    state n: int = 0\n    n\n}\n", "/w/src/b.av": "fn f() -> int { g() }\n"},
            )
            reaches_state(j, "/w/src/b.av", "f")
        }
    }
}

spec "compiler/pure_decl — a top-level state is a place the read-reach sees" {
    given "a fn reading a top-level state, and a caller of it" {
        then "both reach it, so neither is a pure fn" {
            let j = pure_judged({PURE_MAIN: "state n: int = 0\nfn f() -> int { n }\nfn g() -> int { f() }\nfn p() -> int { 1 }\n"})
            reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "f") && reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "g") && !reaches_state(j, PURE_MAIN, "p")
        }
        then "each reaches exactly that one place, as its declaration's key" {
            let j = pure_judged({PURE_MAIN: "state n: int = 0\nfn f() -> int { n }\nfn g() -> int { f() }\n"})
            let at_f = j.state_reaches_of(PURE_MAIN, "f")
            let at_g = j.state_reaches_of(PURE_MAIN, "g")
            at_f.length == 1 && at_g.length == 1 && at_f[0] == at_g[0] && at_f[0].ends_with("\tn")
        }
    }
}
EOF

// A fn's written seats settle with its strongly-connected set, asked of the program layer: a
// cycle takes what a member outside it writes, and a cycle with no writer stays unwritten — so
// its `mut` seats are said never written through.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Judged}

/// The program `main` writes, judged on the layer.
fn writes_judged(main: string) -> Judged {
    held_at({"/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n", "/w/src/main.av": main}, "/w")
        .judged_at("/w/src/main.av")
}

/// Whether the fn `name` writes through its `mut` seat: nothing says it never does.
fn writes_through(j: Judged, name: string) -> bool {
    !j.diagnostics.any((d) -> d.kind == "type.seat_unused" && d.message.contains("`${name}` never writes"))
}

fn writes_cycle(leaf_body: string) -> string {
    "type P = { n: int }\nfn leaf(mut p: P) {\n    ${leaf_body}\n}\nfn ping(mut p: P, k: int) {\n    if k > 0 { pong(p, k - 1) } else { leaf(p) }\n}\nfn pong(mut p: P, k: int) {\n    if k > 0 { ping(p, k - 1) }\n}\nfn quiet(p: P) -> int { p.n }\n"
}

spec "compiler/receivers — a fn's written seats settle with its own set" {
    given "a two-fn cycle whose way out reaches a fn that writes" {
        then "the fn that writes writes the seat" { writes_through(writes_judged(writes_cycle("p.n = 1")), "leaf") }
        then "a caller of it writes the seat" { writes_through(writes_judged(writes_cycle("p.n = 1")), "ping") }
        then "both members of the cycle write the seat" {
            let j = writes_judged(writes_cycle("p.n = 1"))
            writes_through(j, "ping") && writes_through(j, "pong")
        }
    }
    given "the same cycle where nothing writes" {
        then "neither member writes it" {
            let j = writes_judged(writes_cycle("let _ = p.n"))
            !writes_through(j, "ping") && !writes_through(j, "pong")
        }
    }
}
EOF
cat > $T/cancel_scc_test.av <<'EOF'
// A fn's cancel bits settle with its strongly-connected set, asked of the program layer: a cycle
// takes what a member outside it reaches, and a cycle with no waiter reaches nothing.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Judged}

/// The program `main` writes, judged on the layer.
fn cancel_judged(main: string) -> Judged {
    held_at({"/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n", "/w/src/main.av": main}, "/w")
        .judged_at("/w/src/main.av")
}

/// Whether a call to `name` may park.
fn parks(j: Judged, name: string) -> bool { j.cancel_bits(name).starts_with("p") }

fn cancel_cycle(leaf_body: string) -> string {
    "extern fn avra_fiber_sleep(ms: int)\nfn leaf() {\n    ${leaf_body}\n}\nfn ping(k: int) {\n    if k > 0 { pong(k - 1) } else { leaf() }\n}\nfn pong(k: int) {\n    if k > 0 { ping(k - 1) }\n}\nfn quiet() -> int { 1 }\n"
}

spec "compiler/cancel_reach — a fn's cancel bits settle with its own set" {
    given "a two-fn cycle whose way out reaches a fn that parks" {
        then "the fn that parks parks" { parks(cancel_judged(cancel_cycle("avra_fiber_sleep(1)")), "leaf") }
        then "both members of the cycle park" {
            let j = cancel_judged(cancel_cycle("avra_fiber_sleep(1)"))
            parks(j, "ping") && parks(j, "pong")
        }
    }
    given "the same cycle where nothing parks" {
        then "neither member parks" {
            let j = cancel_judged(cancel_cycle("let _ = 1"))
            !parks(j, "ping") && !parks(j, "pong")
        }
    }
}
EOF
cat > $T/seal_order_test.av <<'EOF'
// A `mut` SEAT WRITES THROUGH A RECORD, WHEREVER ITS FN IS DECLARED, asked of the program layer:
// the fn lives in another file than the record and the record holding it, and a write through
// the seat lands in the caller's record.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, Judged}

/// The program over three files: the records, the fn seating one `mut`, and an entry `main`.
fn sealed(main: string) -> Judged {
    held_at(
        {
            "/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"w\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n",
            "/w/src/types.av": "export type Id = { n: int }\nexport type Holder = { id: Id }\n",
            "/w/src/user.av": "use types.{Id}\nexport fn bump(mut x: Id) {\n    x.n = x.n + 1\n}\n",
            "/w/src/main.av": main,
        },
        "/w",
    )
        .judged_at("/w/src/main.av")
}

spec "compiler — a mut seat in another file writes through a record" {
    given "the program" {
        then "it judges clean" { sealed("use types.{Holder}\nuse user.{bump}\nlet h = 1\n").clean() }
    }

        then "a write through it lands in the record" {
            sealed("use types.{Id}\nuse user.{bump}\nmut i = Id { n: 1 }\nbump(i)\ni.n\n").ran() == "2"
        }
        then "and in the record that holds it" {
            sealed("use types.{Id, Holder}\nuse user.{bump}\nmut h = Holder { id: Id { n: 1 } }\nbump(h.id)\nh.id.n\n").ran() == "2"
        }
    }
}
EOF

/// history yet. A lone file has no tree above it and is its own root.
// LICENSED compiler.free_state_verb: a pure PROJECTION — a workspace in, the checkout it stands in out.
fn tree_root(ws: Workspace) -> string { tree_root_of(ws.root, (p: string) -> ws.there(p)) }

/// The checkout `root` stands in, asking `there` what stands at each ancestor.
export fn tree_root_of(root: string, there: fn(string) -> bool) -> string {
    mut manifest_root = root
    mut up = dir_of(root)
    while up != dir_of(up) {
        if there(joined_path(up, ".git")) { return up }
        if there(joined_path(up, "avra.toml")) { manifest_root = up }
        up = dir_of(up)
    }
    manifest_root
}

/// the process from it and keeps the process's blobs in its cache; a host in memory touches
/// neither, so no test writes the machine's cache or moves the tree its keys are spelled from.
fn spelling_tree(root: string, host: Host) -> string {
    let tree = tree_root_of(root, host.exists)
    let machine? = host.cache else { return tree }
    keys_spelled_from(tree)
    blobs_kept_in(machine)

}

/// A two-file library, `b` calling `a`'s `f`.
fn two_file_pkg(name: string) -> string {
    let r = root(name)
    let _ = make_dirs("${r}/src")

--- content ---
//! ONE STORE A CHECKOUT: the program layer keeps its answers under the tree a package stands
//! in — the nearest `.git` above it, else the highest `avra.toml` — so two packages of one
//! tree check into one `.avra-cache`, and the second reuses what the first answered of the
//! library both read. Real subprocesses over a tree minted fresh; `avra_bin`, `scratch_dir`,
//! `hang_bound` and `clean_stdout` are the neighbouring tests' own.
use @std.io.{is_dir, make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.process.{tool, cmd, inherited}
use @std.text.{parse_int}
use @std.time.{stamp}

/// A tree minted fresh: a `.git` at its root, a library, and two programs that read it.
fn store_tree() -> string {
    let root = "${scratch_dir()}/tree_store_${stamp()}"
    let _ = make_dirs("${root}/lib/src")
    let _ = write_text("${root}/.git", "")
    let _ = write_text("${root}/lib/avra.toml", "[package]\nname = \"@t/lib\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")
    let _ = write_text("${root}/lib/src/lib.av", "export fn twice(n: int) -> int { n * 2 }\n")
    for p in ["p1", "p2"] {
        let _ = make_dirs("${root}/${p}/src")
        let _ = write_text(
            "${root}/${p}/avra.toml",
            "[package]\nname = \"${p}\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n\n[dependencies]\n\"@t/lib\" = { path = \"../lib\" }\n",
        )
        let _ = write_text("${root}/${p}/src/main.av", "use @t.lib.{twice}\ntwice(2)\n")
    }
    root
}

/// What `avra check --counts` on the program layer says of the package at `dir`.
fn counted_check(dir: string) -> string {
    let t = match tool(avra_bin()) { .Ok(t) -> t, .Err(_) -> { return "" } }
    clean_stdout(
        (cmd(t, ["check", ".", "--counts"]) with {
            cwd: dir,
            env: inherited().with_var("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET", "0"),
            timeout: hang_bound(),
        })
            .outcome(),
    ) ??
        ""
}

/// The count named `name` a `--counts` line says; -1 where it says none.
fn count_of(said: string, name: string) -> int {
    let at = said.index_of("${name}=")
    if at < 0 { return -1 }
    let rest = said.substring(at + name.length + 1, said.length)
    let end = rest.index_of(" ")
    parse_int(if end < 0 { rest.trim() } else { rest.substring(0, end) }) ?? -1
}

spec "cli — one store a checkout" {
    given "two packages of one tree, each checked once" {
        then "both keep their answers in the tree's one store, and neither in its own" {
            let root = store_tree()
            let _ = counted_check("${root}/p1")
            let _ = counted_check("${root}/p2")
            is_dir("${root}/.avra-cache") && !is_dir("${root}/p1/.avra-cache") && !is_dir("${root}/p2/.avra-cache")
        }
        then "the second reuses what the first answered of the library: it parses only its own file" {
            let root = store_tree()
            let first = counted_check("${root}/p1")
            let second = counted_check("${root}/p2")
            count_of(first, "files_parsed") == 3 && count_of(second, "files_parsed") == 1
        }
    }
}

# A refused pronoun in a derive's own file is never said

`it` binds to the nearest method call, so `fields.any(self.knows(it.name))` hands `it` to
`self.knows`, and is refused (`type.lambda`, `type.mismatch`). In a derive's own package that
refusal is never spoken:

1. `lib/` (a package whose trait `Shown` derives over its own `Part`): `avra check lib` on base56
   (a73903d2, gen-2) — the program layer: `file_generated (… parts.av) was asked while it was being
   answered, under … generator_print -> body_facts -> lowered_method_under -> method_body_typed ->
   package_generated_impls`. The old path (`AVRA_PROGRAM=0`) speaks the refusal. Fix the lambda
   (`(f) -> self.knows(f.name)`) and both check clean. `avra check .` (the root package, a user
   of `lib`) cycles the same way on the program layer, and speaks the refusal on the old path.
   The trigger is the derive running over a type in its OWN package: drop `lib/src/parts.av`
   and both paths speak the refusal.

2. The old path's trap needs std-ui's shape: apply `std-ui-view.patch` to std-ui (tree/view.av, at
   lane commit ff6593fb or later — one line, `self.kept_state(it)` inside `t.fields.find(…)`), then
   `AVRA_PROGRAM=0 avra run std-ui-driver` → `avra: index 1 is out of bounds (length 1)`, and the
   program layer → `generator_print (@std/ui src/tree/view.av ! View) was asked while it was being
   answered`. Without the patch the driver says only its own interp_hole refusal.

type Vocab = { known: List<string> }

impl Vocab {
    fn knows(name: string) -> bool { self.known.contains(name) }

    /// The mistake: `it` binds to the nearest method call, `self.knows(…)`, not to `any`.
    fn any_known(fields: List<Field>) -> bool { fields.any(self.knows(it.name)) }
}

export trait Shown {
    fn shown() -> string

    static fn derive(t: Type) -> Declared {
        let v = Vocab { known: ["id"] }
        let words = if v.any_known(t.fields) { "known" } else { "unknown" }
        Declared { made: [beside(t, quote { impl Shown for ${t} { fn shown() -> string { ${literal(words)} } } })] }
    }
}

file_path: /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/derive_own_file_test.av
--- content ---
// A DERIVE RUN TYPES THE DERIVE FN AND WHAT IT REACHES, NEVER ITS FILE, asked of the program
// layer: a trait whose derive runs over a type of its own package, its derive reaching a method
// whose call is refused. Typing the derive's program asks nothing the derive's runs make, so the
// refusal is spoken where the derive is written — never a cycle through the file it runs over —
// and with the call written right the package checks clean.
use @std.avrac.testing.{held_at, vendored_meta}
use @std.avrac.testing.held.{empty_store}

/// The library whose trait `Shown` derives over its own `Part`, `Vocab.any_known` reading its
/// fields as `pick` writes the predicate.
fn own_derive(pick: string) -> string {
    held_at(
        vendored_meta(
            {
                "/w/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"@repro/shown\"\nversion = \"0.0.1\"\n\n[lib]\nname = \"repro-shown\"\npath = \"src/shown.av\"\n\n[dependencies]\n\"@std/meta\" = { path = \"vendor/meta\" }\n",
                "/w/src/shown.av": "use @std.meta.{Type, Field, Declared, beside, derive, literal}\n\ntype Vocab = { known: List<string> }\n\nimpl Vocab {\n    fn knows(name: string) -> bool { self.known.contains(name) }\n\n    fn any_known(fields: List<Field>) -> bool { fields.any(${pick}) }\n}\n\nexport trait Shown {\n    fn shown() -> string\n\n    static fn derive(t: Type) -> Declared {\n        let v = Vocab { known: [\"id\"] }\n        let words = if v.any_known(t.fields) { \"known\" } else { \"unknown\" }\n        Declared { made: [beside(t, quote { impl Shown for \${t} { fn shown() -> string { \${literal(words)} } } })] }\n    }\n}\n",
                "/w/src/parts.av": "use @std.meta.{derive}\nuse shown.{Shown}\n\n@derive(Shown)\nexport type Part = { id: int }\n",
            },
        ),
        "/w",
    )
        .checked_over(empty_store())
}

spec "compiler/derive — a derive over its own package's type" {
    given "a method call its derive reaches, refused" {
        then "the refusal is spoken, in the derive's own file" {
            let said = own_derive("self.knows(it.name)")
            said.contains("error[type.") && said.contains("shown.av")
        }
        then "and no cycle is asked through the file it runs over" {
            !own_derive("self.knows(it.name)").contains("was asked while it was being answered")
        }
    }
    given "the same call written right" {
        then "the package checks clean" { !own_derive("(f) -> self.knows(f.name)").contains("error[") }
    }
}

```
#!/bin/sh
# THE CHANGED-FILE FMT CHECK — ONE definition, called by the gate's own fmt
# step (.github/workflows/checks.yml) and by `tools/work land`'s local
# preflight, so the two can never drift into two instruments.
#
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>     # the caller has refs (the gate)
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh --files <files…>  # the caller already diffed
#
# Every named `.av` file is run through `fmt --check`. The compiler is
# `${AVRA:-build/avra}` — the tree under test's OWN build. THE BRANCH'S
# COMPILER, NEVER A STALE STANDING ONE: a binary that predates the syntax a
# branch added REFUSES that branch's files and cannot report the canonical
# diff, so it would certify a file the gate then refuses. The gate has its
# own build; a lane's Sprite holds a branch build (`tools/work run`), and its
# synced tree carries no `.git`, which is why `--files` exists. Nothing
# here polls `main`: the refs are named, never watched.
set -eu
[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head> | --files <files…>" >&2; exit 2; }
avra=${AVRA:-build/avra}
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 2; }
if [ "$1" = --files ]; then
    shift
    changed=$*
else
    [ "$#" -eq 2 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>" >&2; exit 2; }
    changed=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "$1" "$2" -- '*.av')
fi
[ -n "$changed" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no changed .av to check"; exit 0; }
"$avra" fmt --check $changed

My new missing/not-text/refused/dangling check (a06c5cdd) made the per-file error count read the whole file text, so every edit re-ran it. Fix in a73b6695: the cause is only asked of a file with no declarations, because a file with any has text. `decl_grain_test` 13/13 and `input_host_test` 13/13. Two caveats:

/// A package minted fresh, `manifest_tail` after its `[package]` table, printing `main` from
/// `src/main.av` and `app` from `src/app.av`.
fn entry_package(name: string, manifest_tail: string) -> string {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""delfn.py FILE NAME... — delete top-level items (fn/type/const/enum/trait/impl X) named NAME, with
their leading /// docs and @annotations. Prints each item's line count; exits 1 if a name is not found."""
import re, sys
path, names = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
L = open(path).read().split('\n')
head = re.compile(r'^(?:export\s+)?(?:static\s+)?(?:fn|type|const|enum|trait|struct)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)')
def span(i):
    s = L[i]; depth = s.count('{') + s.count('(') + s.count('[') - s.count('}') - s.count(')') - s.count(']')
    j = i
    while depth > 0 or (j == i and s.rstrip().endswith(('{', '(', '[', '=', ','))):
        j += 1; t = L[j]
        depth += t.count('{') + t.count('(') + t.count('[') - t.count('}') - t.count(')') - t.count(']')
        if depth <= 0 and t[:1] in '})]': break
    b = i
    while b > 0 and (L[b-1].startswith('///') or L[b-1].startswith('@')): b -= 1
    return b, j
bad = 0; cut = []
for n in names:
    hits = [i for i, s in enumerate(L) if (m := head.match(s)) and m.group(1) == n]
    if not hits: print(f'MISSING {n}'); bad = 1; continue
    for i in hits:
        b, j = span(i); cut.append((b, j)); print(f'{n} {j-b+1}')
keep = set(range(len(L)))
for b, j in cut:
    for k in range(b, j+1): keep.discard(k)
out = [L[k] for k in range(len(L)) if k in keep]
# collapse runs of blank lines
res = []
for s in out:
    if s == '' and res and res[-1] == '': continue
    res.append(s)
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(res))
sys.exit(bad)
EOF

export fn built_binary(args: CliResult) -> Result<string, int> {

        return .Err(1)
    }
    .Ok(binary)

//! THE MULTI-DIAGNOSTIC BUILD FAILURE: a real, two-error program through
//! the actual `avra build` path. `BuildError.Diagnosed` carries the
//! program's own report verbatim, with no Diag wrapper or `caused by:`
//! line ever glued around it — real subprocess, the everyday path, no
//! mocked pieces.
use @std.io.{make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.process.{tool, cmd, Exit, Outcome, ProcessError}

/// A program with two INDEPENDENT, unrelated errors — an undefined call
/// and an undefined type — the shape a clean program most commonly
/// fails with.
fn two_error_program() -> string {
    let _ = make_dirs(scratch_dir())
    let path = "${scratch_dir()}/build_report_two_errors.av"
    let _ = write_text(path, "fn main() {\n    foo()\n    let x: Bar = 1\n}\n")
    path
}

/// The build, run once for every case: each case reads this one real run.
once fn outcome() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    let t = tool(avra_bin())?
    (cmd(t, ["build", two_error_program()]) with { timeout: hang_bound() }).outcome()
}

fn exit_code_1(e: Exit) -> bool {
    match e { .Code(1) -> true, .Code(_) or .Signal(_, _) or .Clean -> false }
}

fn report() -> string {
    match outcome() { .Ok(o) -> o.out.stdout, .Err(_) -> "" }
}

spec "avra build — a real multi-diagnostic failure" {
    given "a program with two independent, unrelated errors" {
        then "the build refuses, exit 1" {
            match outcome() { .Ok(o) -> exit_code_1(o.exit), .Err(_) -> false }

        then "both diagnostics print, each its own error[...] header" {

                report().contains("error[type.unknown]")
        }
        then "nothing wraps the report in a Diag's cause chain — no `caused by:` line at all" {

```
#!/bin/sh
# THE avra COMMAND — the compiler, hosted by itself. `build/avra` is
# the working binary; it rebuilds from `make avra`, which uses the
# binary that is already there. The seed is the cold path, and it is
# taken only when there is no binary at all.
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# THE CALLER'S DIRECTORY, kept before this script moves to the tree's
# root: a command that reads "the package I stand in" (`explain`)
# roots there, never at the tree — `cd` below rewrites PWD too.
AVRA_CWD="$(pwd)"
export AVRA_CWD
# the link flags a manifest writes as ${LLVM_PREFIX}
LLVM_PREFIX="${LLVM_PREFIX:-/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX
# the static LLVM link's platform answers (packages/std-avrac/avra.toml)
if [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ]; then
    AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME="${AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME:-c++}"
    AVRA_SYS_SEARCH="${AVRA_SYS_SEARCH:-/opt/homebrew/lib}"
    export AVRA_SYS_SEARCH
else
    AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME="${AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME:-stdc++}"
fi
export AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME
export AVRA_BOOTSTRAPPING

# A PACKAGE-SCALE RUN — any argument that is a directory — is a
# heavy step: it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs under
# the watchdog (tools/watch.sh), unless it already runs inside one.
# A single-file run is light and runs directly. Judged where the
# caller stands, before the move below.
heavy=0
n=0
for a in "$@"; do n=$((n + 1)); [ "$n" -gt 1 ] && [ -d "$a" ] && heavy=1; done
# A GUARDED PACKAGE RUN IS REFUSED: `AVRA_RC_GUARD` keeps every box that dies so a leak can
# replay its life, which over a package is a machine's worth of memory — it ended a Sprite's
# session. The guard is for one program; `AVRA_GUARDED_PACKAGE=1` takes the cost on purpose.
case "${AVRA_RC_GUARD:-0}" in 0|"") ;; *)
    if [ "$heavy" = 1 ] && [ -z "$AVRA_GUARDED_PACKAGE" ]; then
        echo "avra: AVRA_RC_GUARD keeps every dead box, and a package-scale run makes a machine's worth of them" >&2
        echo "avra:   guard one program — name a file — or set AVRA_GUARDED_PACKAGE=1 to take the cost on purpose." >&2

# KNOWN voice gaps, one TAB-separated line each: a kind or rule, and what
# it lacks (no_witness, no_help, no_fix, no_doc, bad_fix, bad_remedy, no_remedy). This file only ever
# SHRINKS — `avra voices --baseline <this file> --accept` prunes what a
# fix made gone, and no path through it ADDS a line: a new voice gets its
# help, fix and witness in the code, or a human adds the line here,
# reviewed at adoption and every time after. `make voices` gates.
build.failed	no_help
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every kind a voice speaks by literal is a REGISTERED kind.

`refusal`, `warning` and `error_at` take the kind as their first
argument; a literal there that docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md (generated from the
assembled registry by `make witnesses`) has no entry for is a voice that
speaks a kind nothing registered — no row, no summary, no witness, no
help for `avra docs` to find. Reports what it examined."""
import re, sys
import avsrc

CALL = re.compile(r'\b(?:refusal|warning|error_at)\(\s*"([a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+)"')
# The CLI's own failure wrapper is a kind of the program `avra`, never of
# the language the registry describes.
OUTSIDE = {"build.command_failed"}
registered = set(re.findall(r'^## (\S+)$', open('docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md').read(), re.M))
if not registered:
    print("voices-spoken: docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md names no kind — nothing to compare against")
    sys.exit(1)
spoken = {}
files = avsrc.av_files(['packages/*/src'])
for f in files:
    text = open(f).read()
    for m in CALL.finditer(text):
        spoken.setdefault(m.group(1), (f, text[:m.start()].count('\n') + 1))
missing = sorted(k for k in spoken if k not in registered and k not in OUTSIDE)
for k in missing:
    f, line = spoken[k]
    print(f"voices-spoken: `{k}` is spoken at {f}:{line} and no registry row names it")
print(f"voices-spoken: {len(spoken)} spoken kind(s) in {len(files)} file(s) held against {len(registered)} registered")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)

```
file_path: /work/avra/packages/cli/src/commands/tests/check_dir_test.av
--- content ---
//! `avra check <dir>` ON THE PROGRAM LAYER — A CHECK THAT EXAMINED NOTHING IS NO CHECK THAT PASSED.
//! A directory that holds no manifest is no package's root: the check says nothing was checked,
//! names the package it stands in where one does, and leaves by 1. A root without `src/` checks
//! each source file directly in it, as `check <file>` checks it, or — holding none — refuses in
//! `manifest.no_source`'s words. Each case runs the compiler as a user does, its exit and its words.
use @std.io.{make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.time.{stamp}
use @std.process.{tool, cmd, Exit, Outcome, ProcessError}

/// One directory per run, outside any package, so no earlier run's store answers for this one and
/// no `avra.toml` stands above it.
once fn dir_base() -> string { "/tmp/avra-check-dir-test/${stamp()}" }

fn at(name: string) -> string { "${dir_base()}/${name}" }

/// A file at `path` holding `text`, its directory made.
fn put(path: string, text: string) {
    let _ = make_dirs(path.substring(0, path.last_index_of("/") ?? 0))
    let _ = write_text(path, text)
}

fn manifest(name: string) -> string { "[package]\nname = \"${name}\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n" }

const BROKEN: string = "fn f() -> int { nope() }\nf()\n"

/// `check <dir>`, run as a user runs it: its exit and its stdout.
fn checked(dir: string) -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    let t = tool(avra_bin())?
    (cmd(t, ["check", dir]) with { timeout: hang_bound() }).outcome()
}

fn exit_of(o: Result<Outcome, ProcessError>) -> int {
    match o { .Ok(r) -> match r.exit { .Code(n) -> n, .Clean -> 0, .Signal(_, _) -> -1 }, .Err(_) -> -2 }
}

fn said(o: Result<Outcome, ProcessError>) -> string { match o { .Ok(r) -> r.out.stdout, .Err(_) -> "" } }

/// A package `pkg` whose `src/` holds a file that is refused, and a directory under it.
once fn package_dirs() -> string {
    let root = at("pkg")
    put("${root}/avra.toml", manifest("pkg"))
    put("${root}/src/main.av", BROKEN)
    let _ = make_dirs("${root}/src/sub")
    root
}

once fn in_src() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> { checked("${package_dirs()}/src") }

once fn in_sub() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> { checked("${package_dirs()}/src/sub") }

/// A directory of source files that stands in no package.
once fn loose() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    put(at("loose/a.av"), BROKEN)
    checked(at("loose"))
}

/// A package root of one manifest, no `src/`, nothing directly in it.
once fn rootless() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    put(at("rootless/avra.toml"), manifest("rootless"))
    checked(at("rootless"))
}

/// A package root with no `src/` and a refused source file directly in it.
once fn root_direct() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    put(at("direct/avra.toml"), manifest("direct"))
    put(at("direct/a.av"), BROKEN)
    checked(at("direct"))
}

/// The same, its one file clean.
once fn root_direct_clean() -> Result<Outcome, ProcessError> {
    put(at("clean/avra.toml"), manifest("clean"))
    put(at("clean/a.av"), "fn f() -> int { 1 }\nf()\n")
    checked(at("clean"))
}

/// `manifest.no_manifest`'s words for `dir`, naming the package it stands in — the golden.
fn no_manifest_in(dir: string, root: string) -> string {
    "error[manifest.no_manifest]: `${dir}` holds no `avra.toml`: nothing was checked\nhelp: it stands in the package at `${root}`: check that root, or a source file by its path\n"
}

/// The same words for a directory that stands in no package.
fn no_manifest_alone(dir: string) -> string {
    "error[manifest.no_manifest]: `${dir}` holds no `avra.toml`: nothing was checked\nhelp: check a package's root — the directory its `avra.toml` stands in — or a source file by its path\n"
}

spec "avra check <dir> — a directory that is no package's root is never a pass" {
    given "a package's `src/`" {
        then "it is refused: nothing was checked, the package's root named" {
            said(in_src()) == no_manifest_in("${package_dirs()}/src", package_dirs())
        }
        then "and the check leaves by 1" { exit_of(in_src()) == 1 }
    }
    given "a directory under a package's `src/`" {
        then "it is refused, naming the same root" {
            said(in_sub()) == no_manifest_in("${package_dirs()}/src/sub", package_dirs())
        }
        then "and leaves by 1" { exit_of(in_sub()) == 1 }
    }
    given "a directory of source files in no package" {
        then "it is refused, and no root is named" { said(loose()) == no_manifest_alone(at("loose")) }
        then "and leaves by 1" { exit_of(loose()) == 1 }
    }
    given "a package root with no `src/` and nothing directly in it" {
        then "it is refused in manifest.no_source's words" {
            said(rootless()) ==
                "error[manifest.no_source]: nothing to check under `${at("rootless")}`: no `src/` and no program files\nhelp: add a `src/` directory, or a `.av` file directly under this root\n"
        }
        then "and leaves by 1" { exit_of(rootless()) == 1 }
    }
    given "a package root with no `src/` and a source file directly in it" {
        then "the file is checked, and what it is refused with is said" {
            said(root_direct()).contains("error[resolve.unresolved]") && exit_of(root_direct()) == 1
        }
        then "a clean one is checked clean, by 0" { exit_of(root_direct_clean()) == 0 }
    }
    given "a package's own root" {
        then "it is checked as it always was, its file's refusal said" {
            let o = checked(package_dirs())
            said(o).contains("error[resolve.unresolved]") && !said(o).contains("manifest.no_manifest") && exit_of(o) == 1
        }
    }
}

export type RecordSignature = { type_params: List<string>, fields: List<FieldSeat>, bounds: List<SignedType?> = [] }

/// The signature of the record (or component) `file` declares as `name`, absent when it declares
/// none: a component holding a body carries what its composing trait names past its own fields.
@query

the record's own module's generators make of a name it doesn't write — the very answer being made
— and the sites and arguments a generator is handed read `file_scope` whole. With F1's files gone
the build was five cycles (`generated_names` … `record_signature -> resolved`) and no names.

A generator's inputs read the written stratum: the meta values it is handed (item_meta) and `@std/
meta`'s `Fn` slots sign records through `record_signature_written` — its spreads and a composed
trait's record in the same stratum — and the sites and arguments in item_generators/item_generated
read `written_file_scope` through `stratum_resolved`, which binds a pending import as that name is
read. Asking a module's generated names while they are made only ever cycled, so nothing that
answered before answers otherwise; what cycled is now refused.

Witness: generator_strata_test 4/4, derive_own_file_test 3/3, item_scope_test 9/9,
item_scope_adversarial_test 25/25.

fn impls_filed(engine: QueryEngine, package: string, generated: bool) -> AnswerParts {
    mut by_type: Map<string, List<FiledImpl>> = {}
    for path in package_sources(engine, package, "src") {
        let f = SourceFileAddress { package_name: package, path_in_package: path }
        let first = if generated { item_count(engine, f) } else { 0 }
        let by_item = if generated { generated_impls(engine, f) } else { written_impls(engine, f) }
        for at, held in by_item {
            for nth, i in held {
                let d? = impl_target(engine, f, i) else { continue }
                let tr = if i.implements == null { null } else { impl_named(engine, f, i.trait_in, i.implements!) }
                let filed = FiledImpl {
                    at: ImplAt {
                        file: f,
                        item: first + at,
                        params: impl_params(engine, i, d),
                        nth: nth,
                    },
                    of: d.file,
                    methods: i.methods,
                    statics: i.statics,
                    implements: if tr == null { null } else { TraitAt { file: tr!.file, name: tr!.name } },
                }
                by_type.set(d.name, (by_type.get(d.name) ?? []).concat([filed]))
            }
        }
    }
    answer_parts(
        [NamedValue { name: name, value: Filed { impls: held }.saved_bytes() } for name, held in by_type],
    )
}

/// What each generated item of a file keeps for its words, in the order made.
fn generated_abouts(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<ItemAbout> {
    [about_of(g.tape.about) for g in file_generated(engine, file).items]
}

/// How two generated items differ, where their nodes stand and the files that wrote them aside: the
/// first statement and method that mean something else; absent when alike.
export fn item_difference(one: SyntaxTape, other: SyntaxTape) -> string? {
    let ours = unhomed(one)
    let theirs = unhomed(other)
    if ours.tape.meaning_hash.same_as(theirs.tape.meaning_hash) { return null }
    if ours.stmts.length != theirs.stmts.length { return "${ours.stmts.length} statements, the other's ${theirs.stmts.length}" }
    for j, s in ours.stmts {
        let t = theirs.stmts[j]
        if ours.store.stmt_fingerprint(s) == theirs.store.stmt_fingerprint(t) { continue }
        return "statement ${j}${method_differing(ours.store, s, theirs.store, t)} means something else"
    }
    "its meaning, though every statement's fingerprint agrees"
}

/// An item read back with every node's file dropped, and its tape written again.
type Unhomed = { store: SyntaxArena, stmts: List<StmtId>, tape: SyntaxTape }

export fn built_binary(args: CliResult) -> Result<string, int> {
    let path? = slotted_path(args) else { return .Err(2) }
    let target = args.option("target")
    let tools = if target == "" {
        null
    } else {
        match toolchain_with(
            host_lookup(),
            target,
            args.has_flag("wasm_reactor"),
            args.has_flag("wasm_debug"),
            !args.has_flag("no_wasm_fallback"),
        ) { .Ok(t) -> t, .Err(code) -> { return .Err(code) } }
    }
    let net = net_said([path], NetJudge.Build)
    let built = if is_a_dir(path) { program_built(path, timed(args), tools, net, args.has_flag("release")) } else { program_file_built(path, timed(args), tools, net, args.has_flag("release")) }
    let binary = match built { .Ok(b) -> b, .Err(code) -> { return .Err(code) } }
    if !exists_at(binary) {
        eprintln("avra: the program layer wrote no binary at ${binary}")
        return .Err(1)
    }
    .Ok(binary)
}

// `avra check` AS A USER RUNS IT, ON THE PROGRAM LAYER: what the cli's check tests hold, now that
// the old path's in-process `checked_at` is gone. The compiler runs as a child with the net off — the
// check that stands once the old path goes — from `/`, so a path it says reads as its fixture's own.
use @std.process.{tool, cmd, inherited}

/// What a check said that passed: its warnings, as stdout carries them, and whether the store
/// answered it whole — every answer it read kept from a check before (`time: check · cache hit`).
type LayerChecked = { warnings: string, reused: bool }

/// `avra check <path>` on the program layer: what it said where it passed, else its refusal.
fn layer_checked(path: string, more: List<string> = []) -> Result<LayerChecked, string> {
    let t = match tool(avra_bin()) { .Ok(t) -> t, .Err(e) -> { return .Err("no compiler: ${e.describe().message}") } }
    let run = (cmd(t, ["check", path, "--time"].concat(more)) with {
        cwd: "/",
        env: inherited().with_var("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET", "0"),
        timeout: hang_bound(),
        ok_exits: [0, 1, 2],
    })
        .outcome()
    match run {
        .Ok(o) -> {
            let said = rooted_said(o.out.stdout)
            match o.exit {
                .Code(0) or .Clean -> .Ok(LayerChecked { warnings: said, reused: o.out.stderr.contains("time: check · cache hit") }),
                .Code(_) or .Signal(_, _) -> .Err(said),
            }
        },
        .Err(e) -> .Err("the check did not run: ${e.describe().message}"),
    }
}

/// What a check run from `/` said, each fixture path it names whole again — the child renders

/// What a check of `root`'s app warns, its root spelled out of it.
fn wo_warned(root: string) -> string? {
    match layer_checked("${root}/app") {
        .Ok(c) -> c.warnings.replace(root, "<root>"),
        .Err(_) -> null,
    }
}

/// A warm check after a body edit, beside a cold check of the edited tree.
fn wo_pair() -> List<string?> {
    let warm = wo_tree("warm", "k(1)")
    let _ = wo_warned(warm)
    let _ = write_text("${warm}/app/src/main.av", "use @x.lib.{k}\nexport fn f() -> int { k(2) }\n")
    [wo_warned(warm), wo_warned(wo_tree("cold", "k(2)"))]
}

spec "commands/check warm order" {
    given "a body edit in an app over a dependency with warnings" {

            let both = wo_pair()
            both[0] != null && both[0] == both[1] && both[0]!.contains("lib/src/main.av")
        }
    }
}

/// LLVM as its one shared library where it stands; and the program as two shared objects — the

/// What a build of the package at `root` asks, as `engine` reads it.
fn binary_asked(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    disk: Disk,
    bin: string,
    stem: string,
    mode: BuildMode,
    tools: Toolchain?,
) -> BinaryAsked {
    let t? = tools else { return native_asked(engine, disk, bin, stem, mode) }
    let words = phased(engine, "link words", () -> linked_words(engine, disk, false, t.target))
    BinaryAsked {
        entry: disk.file_at(bin),
        compiler: compiler_identity(),
        head: wasm_link_head(t.target, t.reactor, t.debug),
        words: words,
        linked: linked_digests(words.concat([t.runtime])),
        dir: joined_path(disk.root, "${BUILD_DIR}-${t.target}"),
        opt: mode.opt,
        layered: false,
        inlined: inlines_runtime(),
        target: t.target,
        runtime: t.runtime,
        linker: t.linker,
        wasm_opt: t.wasm_opt,
        fallback: t.fallback && t.wasm_opt != "",
    }
}

/// Where a build keeps its objects and binaries, under its package: a non-host target's beside it,
/// named for the target, so a native build and a wasm one never share an object or a binary.
const BUILD_DIR: string = ".avra-cache/tapes-build"

/// What a native build of the program `bin` on `disk`, placed at `stem`, asks in `mode`. A program
/// that defines a host fn links whole whatever its mode: a host calls it by the bare symbol in the
/// binary it loads, and a layered binary holds none of the program's code.
fn native_asked(engine: QueryEngine, disk: Disk, bin: string, stem: string, mode: BuildMode) -> BinaryAsked {
            target: target,
            runtime: runtime,
            linker: linker,
            wasm_opt: wasm_opt,
            fallback: fallback,
            placed: placed,
        },
    )
    match made { .Linked(kept, stood) -> BuiltBinary.Linked(file_name(kept), stood), rest -> made }
}
