--- content ---
// A KEPT BINARY IS A FUNCTION OF THE TOOLS THAT LINKED IT. A build on the program layer asks for its
// binary by every tool its link runs, each by its identity (`tools_marked`: its path, and the disk's
// mark of what stands there), so a binary stands only while those tools stand as they did: the C
// compiler or the linker replaced in place — a new build of clang, an upgraded lld — is another
// question, and the binary is linked again. Each build runs as a user's does, a process of its own,
// the two sharing only the store; the tools are wrappers the test owns, first on the PATH.
use @std.io.{env, make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.path.{dir_of, joined_path}
use @std.time.{stamp}
use @std.process.{tool, cmd, inherited}

/// One directory per run, so no earlier run's store answers for this one.
once fn run_base() -> string { "/tmp/avra-build-tools-test/${stamp()}" }

/// A program of one line.
fn program(name: string) -> string {
    let r = "${run_base()}/${name}"
    let _ = make_dirs("${r}/src")
    let _ = write_text("${r}/avra.toml", "[package]\nname = \"${name}\"\nversion = \"0.0.1\"\n")
    let _ = write_text("${r}/src/main.av", "1 + 1\n")
    r
}

/// The real tool `word` stands for: the one the PATH finds; `ld.lld` beside `clang` where it stands
/// there, as the link looks for it.
fn real_tool(word: string) -> string {
    let cc = match tool("clang") { .Ok(t) -> t.path, .Err(_) -> "" }
    if word == "ld.lld" {
        let beside = joined_path(dir_of(cc), "ld.lld")
        let found = match tool(beside) { .Ok(t) -> t.path, .Err(_) -> "" }
        if found != "" { return found }
        return match tool("ld.lld") { .Ok(t) -> t.path, .Err(_) -> "" }
    }
    cc
}

/// A directory of wrappers, one for `clang` and one for `ld.lld`, each running the real tool; `extra`
/// lines appended to `ld.lld`'s, so a wrapper rewritten with more of them is a linker replaced in place.
fn wrappers(name: string, cc_extra: string = "", ld_extra: string = "") -> string {
    let dir = "${run_base()}/${name}-tools"
    let _ = make_dirs(dir)
    wrote(joined_path(dir, "clang"), real_tool("clang"), cc_extra)
    wrote(joined_path(dir, "ld.lld"), real_tool("ld.lld"), ld_extra)
    dir
}

/// The wrapper at `path` running `real`, with `extra` lines, made executable.
fn wrote(path: string, real: string, extra: string) {
    let _ = write_text(path, "#!/bin/sh\n${extra}exec ${real} \"$@\"\n")
    let t = match tool("chmod") { .Ok(t) -> t, .Err(_) -> { return } }
    let _ = cmd(t, ["+x", path]).outcome()
}

/// Whether `avra build <r>` with the wrappers in `tools` first on the PATH found its binary standing
/// (`time: lower+emit · cache hit`); absent where the build failed.
fn stood(r: string, tools: string) -> bool? {
    let t = match tool(avra_bin()) { .Ok(t) -> t, .Err(_) -> { return null } }
    let run = (cmd(t, ["build", r, "--time"]) with {
        env: inherited().with_var("PATH", "${tools}:${env("PATH") ?? ""}").with_var("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET", "0"),
        timeout: hang_bound(),
        ok_exits: [0, 1, 2],
    })
        .outcome()
    match run {
        .Ok(o) -> match o.exit {
            .Code(0) or .Clean -> o.out.stderr.contains("time: lower+emit · cache hit"),
            rest -> null,
        },
        .Err(_) -> null,
    }
}

spec "cli build — a kept binary is a function of the tools that linked it" {
    given "a program built twice, its tools standing as they did" {
        then "the second build finds the first's binary standing" {
            let r = program("same")
            let tools = wrappers("same")
            let _ = stood(r, tools)
            stood(r, tools) == true
        }
    }
    given "the linker replaced in place by one of a different size" {
        then "the binary is linked again" {
            let r = program("ld-moved")
            let tools = wrappers("ld-moved")
            let _ = stood(r, tools)
            let _ = wrappers("ld-moved", "", "# a linker of another build\n")
            stood(r, tools) == false
        }
        then "and the build after that stands on the new linker" {
            let r = program("ld-moved-again")
            let tools = wrappers("ld-moved-again")
            let _ = stood(r, tools)
            let _ = wrappers("ld-moved-again", "", "# a linker of another build\n")
            let _ = stood(r, tools)
            stood(r, tools) == true
        }
    }
    given "the C compiler replaced in place" {
        then "the binary is linked again" {
            let r = program("cc-moved")
            let tools = wrappers("cc-moved")
            let _ = stood(r, tools)
            let _ = wrappers("cc-moved", "# a compiler of another build\n", "")
            stood(r, tools) == false
        }
    }
}

//! `compiler/idioms.av`'s own rules are declared as `quote { ... } -> ...` patterns whose left side,
//! matched structurally, is a `Pat.Quote` — and that pattern's own text is a CODE SHAPE
//! (`${cx}.emit(Ins.IfStart(${c}))`, say) mirrored into an expr tree so the pattern can be WRITTEN.
//! Before the rules pass learned to stop at a `Pat.Quote`, it walked INTO that mirrored tree as into
//! any other code, so every rule in this file matched its OWN declaration — a PRECISION bug
//! (avra-8sb5.25.49): `compiler/idioms.av` had 34 self-matches and exactly one real defect
//! (`most_copied`'s own `mut best: string? = null`, a genuine `nullable_flag_local`). Both halves
//! are held here, on the program layer, over the real std-avrac package as it stands on disk: no
//! rule fires on its own pattern, and the one real defect still fires.
use @std.avrac.testing.held.{held_on_disk}

/// Each rule finding the program layer makes in `compiler/idioms.av`, judged as part of the real
/// std-avrac package.
once fn idioms_findings() -> List<string> {
    let root = "${tree_root()}/packages/std-avrac"
    let j = held_on_disk(root).judged_at("${root}/src/compiler/idioms.av")
    [f.rule for f in j.findings() if f.file.ends_with("compiler/idioms.av")]
}

spec "commands/rule pass — a rule never fires on its own pattern" {
    given "compiler/idioms.av, judged as part of the real std-avrac package" {
        then "no rule fires on one of the file's own quote patterns: one finding, never 35" {
            idioms_findings().length == 1
        }
        then "and the one real defect still fires" { idioms_findings() == ["nullable.nullable_flag_local"] }
    }
}

/// What makes a program's objects besides its own answers: the compiler that emits them,
/// the backend's code, as the build's own code hash, the level they are emitted at, whether the
/// runtime's hot leaves are inlined, and the runtime and archives it links. Every key a build's
/// objects make — each object's, its link's, a layered link's — holds it.
fn objects_salt(engine: QueryEngine, asked: BinaryAsked) -> List<string> {
    [
        asked.compiler,
        binary_question(engine, asked).code_hash,
        asked.opt,
        if asked.inlined { "inlined" } else { "calls" },
        asked.target,
    ]
        .concat(asked.linked)
}

# A DERIVE'S NEW MEMBERS ARE SEEN ON THE NEXT CHECK. A package's own trait derives `first` beside a
# type, through `beside(t, quote { impl ${t} { … } })`; a test of that package passes; a second member
# is added inside the quoted impl, and the test calling it is run again over the same machine cache:

# machine cache) keeps the deriving module's record, and a member added inside a quoted impl moves

import re
p='/work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/interface.av'; s=open(p).read(); L=s.split('\n')
head=re.compile(r'^(?:export\s+)?(?:fn|type|const)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)')
def span_item(i):
    # an item starting at line i (0-based) with its leading docs: to the line closing it
    b=i
    while b>0 and (L[b-1].startswith('//') or L[b-1].startswith('@')): b-=1
    s=L[i]; depth=s.count('{')+s.count('(')+s.count('[')-s.count('}')-s.count(')')-s.count(']'); j=i
    while depth>0:
        j+=1; t=L[j]; depth+=t.count('{')+t.count('(')+t.count('[')-t.count('}')-t.count(')')-t.count(']')
    return b,j
names=['NO_ORDINAL','wire_key','WireName','MAKER_MARK','wire_spelled','WireDeclRef']
spans=[]
for i,l in enumerate(L):
    m=head.match(l)
    if m and m.group(1) in names: spans.append(span_item(i))
    if l.startswith('impl Decls {'):
        b=i
        while L[b-1].startswith('//'): b-=1
        j=i
        while L[j]!='}': j+=1
        spans.append((b,j))
spans.sort(); print(len(spans), [(a+1,b+1) for a,b in spans])
# import block: from first 'use' to the line before first doc/type after imports
ui=[i for i,l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith('use ')]
imp_end=ui[-1]
while not L[imp_end].rstrip().endswith('}') and not (L[imp_end].startswith('use ') and '{' not in L[imp_end]): imp_end+=1
imports='\n'.join(L[ui[0]:imp_end+1])
moved='\n\n'.join('\n'.join(L[a:b+1]) for a,b in spans)
out='''//! A DECLARATION'S WIRE AND A TYPE'S SYMBOL, as the program layer's lowering and a declaration's
//! durable fold spell them: the `Decls` verbs that name a declaration or a type the same way in
//! every process, apart from the old Workspace's interface they were written beside.
'''+imports+'\n\n'+moved+'\n'
open('/work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/decl_wires.av','w').write(out)
keep=set(range(len(L)))
for a,b in spans:
    for k in range(a,b+1): keep.discard(k)
rest=[L[k] for k in range(len(L)) if k in keep]
res=[]
for x in rest:
    if x=='' and res and res[-1]=='': continue
    res.append(x)
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(res))
print('decl_wires lines', out.count('\n'))
EOF

/// What the old path says of `source`, read whole and its workspace let go before the program
/// layer derives anything: one derivation is alive at a time.
fn old_said(source: string) -> OldSaid {
    let a = analyze_source(source)

        said: if quiet { run_refusal(ran) } else { said_sorted(a.diagnostics) },
        run: run_said(ran, quiet),
        quiet: quiet,
    }
    one_shot_let_go()
    said

/// What a run that refused says, as a diagnostic is said: the old path refuses at run what the layer

/// refusal no kind heads.
fn run_refusal(r: Result<string, string>) -> string {
    let e? = match r { .Err(e) -> e, .Ok(_) -> null } else { return "" }

    let close = head.index_of("]: ")
    if close < 0 { return "" }
    "${head.substring(6, close)}: ${head.substring(close + 3, head.length)}"
}

}

/// A program's printed value, or "<refused>".
export fn shown(source: string) -> string {
    judged(source).ran() ?? "<refused>"
}

/// The source projected through the printer's canonical form — "<parse
/// refused>" when it does not parse. Two test files carried this
/// byte-identical.
export fn projected(source: string) -> string {
    let p = parse_source(source)
    if !p.voices.list.is_empty() { return "<parse refused>" }
    render_source(p.store, p.stmts)
}

/// How many diagnostics one program earns. The COUNT is half of a
/// refusal test: a cascade hides behind `contains` alone.
export fn refusals(source: string) -> int {
    judged(source).diagnostics.length
}

/// A program refused EXACTLY ONCE, saying `phrase`. The count is not
/// optional here — one mistake earns one message, so a refusal test
/// that does not pin the count cannot catch a cascade. 131 sites
/// spelled this by hand, and the ones that wrote `>= 1` instead were
/// asserting almost nothing.
export fn refused_with(source: string, phrase: string) -> bool {
    let a = judged(source)
    a.diagnostics.length == 1 && a.report().contains(phrase)
}

/// A program that refuses to RUN, saying `phrase`: the evaluator's refusal of a program its build
/// accepts, or the one thing its build says of what it runs before any program does — a const's
/// settling — and never a cascade.
export fn refused_at_run(source: string, phrase: string) -> bool {
    let a = judged(source)
    if a.diagnostics.length > 1 { return false }
    match a.run() { .Err(msg) -> msg.contains(phrase), .Ok(_) -> false }
}

/// One module of a test program: its name and its one file's text.
export type Module = { name: string, text: string }

impl Module {
    fn path() -> string { "/w/src/${self.name}/${self.name}.av" }
}

/// What a program answers when run, or the words it stopped with.
export fn answered(p: Judged) -> string {
    match p.run() { .Ok(v) -> v, .Err(why) -> why }
}

fn unsound(s: Shown) -> bool {
    let text = match s.witness {
        .Source(t) -> t,
        .Package(_) or .Built(_) or .Unread(_, _) or .Absent or .Beyond(_) -> "",
    }
    if text.is_empty() { return false }
    let drawn = [d for d in avra().analyze(new_source_file("witness.av", text)).diagnostics if d.kind == s.code.kind]
    [spliced_fails(s.code.kind, text, d, sg) for d in drawn for sg in d.suggestions].any(it)
}

fn spliced_fails(kind: string, text: string, d: Diag, sg: Suggestion) -> bool {
    let after? = spliced(text, sg.edits) else { return true }
    let out = avra().check(new_source_file("witness.av", after))
    unreadable(out) || out.contains("[${kind}]: ${d.message}")
}

    files: Map<string, string> = {},
) -> bool {
    let roots = example_roots(example_files(before, files))
    let hit? = nearest_fix_in(applied, roots) else { return false }
    let text? = hit.rendered() else { return false }
    same_fingerprint(text, after)
}

/// Whether `applied` fixes nothing in `before`.
export fn checks_keeps(applied: fn(Code) -> Fix?, before: string) -> bool {
    nearest_fix_in(applied, example_roots(example_files(before, {}))) == null
}

/// Whether the delete `applied` makes of `before`, spliced as the layer's own fix splices it
/// (`held_delete_edits`), leaves a program the layer judges clean.
export fn checks_delete(applied: fn(Code) -> Fix?, before: string, files: Map<string, string> = {}) -> bool {
    let rfs = example_files(before, files)
    let hit? = nearest_fix_in(applied, example_roots(rfs)) else { return false }
    if deleted(hit) == null { return false }
    let found? = example_roots(rfs).find((c) -> nearest_fix(applied, c) != null) else { return false }
    let edits = held_delete_edits(found.of, hit_at(hit, found))
    if edits.is_empty() { return false }
    let after? = spliced(before, edits) else { return false }
    example_held(after, files).judged_at(example_main(files)).clean()
}

/// Where the fix `hit` stands: the code it was made at.
fn hit_at(_hit: Fix, at: Code) -> At { at.at }

/// Whether two sources' examples fingerprint alike.
fn same_fingerprint(rendered: string, after: string) -> bool {
    let r? = example_fp(example_files(rendered, {})) else { return false }
    let a? = example_fp(example_files(after, {})) else { return false }
    r == a
}

    PlacedDiag,
> {

        reads_the_file,

export fn tree_root_of(root: string, there: fn(string) -> bool) -> string {
    if there(joined_path(root, ".git")) { return root }
    mut manifest_root = root
    mut up = dir_of(root)
    while up != dir_of(up) {
        if there(joined_path(up, ".git")) { return up }
        if there(joined_path(up, "avra.toml")) { manifest_root = up }
        up = dir_of(up)
    }
    manifest_root
}

import re,sys
KEEP=set("Package family_code_hash reads_of Reads Spelled trapped BuildOutcome Toolchain Shaped Chain Raised parse_program Parsed Subject Counted Reached Uses head_of unmarked row_wait_said spawn_wait_said RefusesCall ChildEnd SuiteProgram in_scope proofs_said quarrel admission entering dep_chain Admitting unset_link_holes_of Looked Analysis one_shot_let_go Application fix_applied fighting_pair rule_doc fixable repairable errors_spoken swallowed_break kept_seats deleted decl_span deletion_edit Signed cleanup_unbounded file_text parse_said rule_examples LinkWorld manifest_library manifest_link_words manifest_wasm_words host_fn_shadowing".split())
OLDFILES=set("workspace record expand workspace_analysis build voices whole derive verdict failures program cache_walk references producers cancel_reach suite packages world analysis rule_fix consumes rule_delete signed cleanup answers parse_said".split())
log=open(sys.argv[1]).read().split('\n')
sites={}
for i,l in enumerate(log):
    if l.startswith('error['):
        for k in range(i+1,i+4):
            m=re.search(r'╭─\[(/work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/([a-z_]+)\.av):(\d+):',log[k])
            if m:
                if m.group(2) in OLDFILES: sites.setdefault(m.group(1),set()).add(int(m.group(3)))
                break
head=re.compile(r'^(?:export\s+)?(?:once\s+)?(?:fn|type|const|enum|trait|impl)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)')
def strip(t):
    out=[];q=False;e=False
    for ch in t:
        if q:
            if e: e=False
            elif ch=='\\': e=True
            elif ch=='"': q=False
            continue
        if ch=='"': q=True; continue
        if ch=='/' and out and out[-1]=='/': out.pop(); break
        out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)
for p,lines in sites.items():
    L=open(p).read().split('\n'); kill=set(); 
    for ln in sorted(lines):
        i=ln-1
        while i>=0 and not head.match(L[i]): i-=1
        if i<0: continue
        name=head.match(L[i]).group(1)
        if name in KEEP: print('KEEP-ERR', p.split('/')[-1], ln, name); continue
        if L[i].startswith('impl '): print('IMPL-ERR', p.split('/')[-1], ln, L[i][:60]); continue
        # span
        b=i
        while b>0 and (L[b-1].startswith('//') or L[b-1].startswith('@')): b-=1
        d=0; j=i; ang=False
        while True:
            t=strip(L[j]); d+=t.count('{')+t.count('(')+t.count('[')-t.count('}')-t.count(')')-t.count(']')
            if t.rstrip().endswith('<'): ang=True
            if t.startswith('>'): ang=False
            if d<=0 and not ang and (j>i or not t.rstrip().endswith(('=',','))): break
            j+=1
        kill.update(range(b,j+1)); print('cut', p.split('/')[-1], name, j-b+1)
    out=[L[k] for k in range(len(L)) if k not in kill]
    res=[]
    for x in out:
        if x=='' and res and res[-1]=='': continue
        res.append(x)
    open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(res))
EOF

    }

    /// ONE IS ALIVE AT A TIME: its rows stand in the process until its

        ws.alone()
        let a = ws.analysis(ws.file_id(src.file))
        ws.disarmed()
        a
    }

}

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn
…[431 chars cut]…
ra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
```

/// checkout keeps its packages beside `build/`, an install keeps them
/// under `lib/avra/std/`, and a binary a checkout's own package built —
/// a suite, a tool — stands beneath that checkout's `packages/`. Null
/// when none stands — a bare binary with no std beside it, which
/// resolves what its manifests declare and nothing more.
fn std_root() -> string? { std_roots().find(is_dir(it)) }

/// Where the toolchain's std may stand for this binary: beside a checkout's `build/`, under an
/// install's `lib/`, then each `packages` directory above it.
fn std_roots() -> List<string> {
    toolchain_files(["../packages", "../lib/avra/std"])
        .concat(packages_above(normalized(avra_self_dir())))
}

/// Each directory named `packages` at or above `dir`, nearest first.
fn packages_above(dir: string) -> List<string> {
    if dir.length <= 1 { return [] }
    if file_name(dir) == "packages" { [dir] } else { [] }.concat(packages_above(dir_of(dir)))
}

impl Language {
    /// The whole pipeline over ONE file — a program of one: its own
    /// declarations are its scope, and a `use` has no package to
    /// reach.
    ///
    /// ONE IS ALIVE AT A TIME: its rows stand in the process until its
    /// workspace is let go, and nothing but the next analysis knows the
    /// last one is done with — so the next lets it go.
    fn analyze(src: SourceFile) -> Analysis {
        one_shot_let_go()
        let ws = lone_workspace(src.file, src.text, self)
        ws.alone()
        let a = ws.analysis(ws.file_id(src.file))
        ws.disarmed()
        a
    }

}

/// ONE ONE-SHOT WORKSPACE IS ALIVE AT A TIME: its rows stand in the
/// process until it is let go, and nothing but the next one knows the last
/// is done with — so the next lets it go BEFORE it is made, and two never
/// stand at once.
export fn one_shot_let_go() {
    for prior in standing_one_shot().get() { prior.superseded() }
    let none: List<Workspace> = []
    standing_one_shot().set(none)
}

/// Whether a workspace stands, or was let go — by its holder, or by the
/// next one-shot workspace made after it.
export enum Stand { Open, LetGo, Superseded }

/// What a read through a workspace that does not stand is refused with.
fn stand_voice(s: Stand) -> string {
    match s {
        .Open -> standing_refused(),

}

//! `avra diagnostics` — the error index, made: every registered code,
//! the source that triggers it, and the compiler's own words over
//! that source. Refuses when a witness no longer produces its code —
//! the golden would then pin whatever it produces instead.
use @std.cli.{CliResult, Runnable, command}
use @std.avrac.compiler.dev.{
    diagnostics_index,
    shadowed_witnesses,
    shown_codes,
    silent_witnesses,
    stray_witnesses,
    unwitnessed,
}

type DiagnosticsCmd = {}

impl Runnable for DiagnosticsCmd {
    fn run(args: CliResult) -> int {
        let runs = shown_codes()
        println(diagnostics_index(runs))
        let silent = silent_witnesses(runs)
        for s in silent { drifted(s.code.kind) }
        for id in stray_witnesses() { stray(id) }
        for id in shadowed_witnesses() { shadowed(id) }
        coverage_said(runs.length, [s for s in runs if s.fired].length, unwitnessed(runs).length)
        if silent.is_empty() && stray_witnesses().is_empty() && shadowed_witnesses().is_empty() { 0 } else { 1 }
    }
}

cat > /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/10f70e18-c27a-5319-9026-e2ec24ef6325/scratchpad/reach.py <<'EOF'
# reach.py <root-dir> [names...]: over-approximate liveness of top-level declarations in packages/*/src.
# A decl is live if a root's text (or a live decl's text) names it by word. Over-approximate on purpose:
# what it calls dead is dead. Prints the dead decls of std-avrac by file, or for each name asked, live/dead.
import os, re, sys
root = sys.argv[1]; asked = sys.argv[2:]
DECL = re.compile(r'^(?:export\s+)?(?:once\s+|mut\s+|static\s+)*(fn|type|enum|const|rule|fact_rule|collect|identity|trait|grammar|ctx|state)\s+(?:enum\s+)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)', re.M)
WORD = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*')
decls = {}   # name -> list of (file, text)
roots_text = []
for pkgdir, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(root, 'packages')):
    if '/vendor' in pkgdir or '/.std' in pkgdir: continue
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.av'): continue
        p = os.path.join(pkgdir, f); t = open(p, errors='replace').read()
        rel = os.path.relpath(p, root)
        in_avrac = rel.startswith('packages/std-avrac/')
        is_test = '/tests/' in rel or f.endswith('_test.av')
        if not in_avrac or is_test:
            roots_text.append(t); continue
        # split the file into top-level chunks at column-0 declarations / impls / annotations
        lines = t.split('\n'); chunks = []; cur = []; ann = False
        for l in lines:
            if re.match(r'^(export\s+|impl\b|@|fn |type |enum |const |rule |fact_rule |collect |once |identity |trait |grammar |spec |use |ctx |state )', l) and not (cur and cur[-1].startswith('@')):
                if cur: chunks.append(cur)
                cur = [l]
            else: cur.append(l)
        if cur: chunks.append(cur)
        for c in chunks:
            text = '\n'.join(c)
            head = [l for l in c if not l.startswith('@') and not l.startswith('///')]
            first = head[0] if head else ''
            annotated = any(l.startswith('@') for l in c)
            if first.startswith('impl') :
                # methods: each `fn name` inside the impl is a node of its own, named by the method name
                for m in re.finditer(r'^    (?:export\s+)?(?:mut\s+|static\s+)*fn\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)', text, re.M):
                    decls.setdefault(m.group(1), []).append((rel, text, False))
                # the impl's target/trait words are read by the impl itself
                continue
            m = DECL.match(first)
            if not m:
                if first.startswith('use ') or first.startswith('spec ') or first.strip()=='' : 
                    if first.startswith('spec '): roots_text.append(text)
                    continue
                roots_text.append(text); continue
            kind, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            rootish = annotated or kind in ('rule', 'fact_rule', 'collect')
            decls.setdefault(name, []).append((rel, text, rootish))
            if rootish: roots_text.append(text)
live = set(); work = []
def mark(text):
    for w in set(WORD.findall(text)):
        if w in decls and w not in live:
            live.add(w); work.append(w)
for t in roots_text: mark(t)
while work:
    w = work.pop()
    for (_, text, _) in decls[w]: mark(text)
if asked:
    for a in asked: print(f"{a}: {'LIVE' if a in live else ('DEAD' if a in decls else 'gone')}  {sorted(set(r for r,_,_ in decls.get(a,[])))}")
else:
    dead = {}
    for n, ds in decls.items():
        if n in live: continue
        for (r, _, _) in ds: dead.setdefault(r, []).append(n)
    for r in sorted(dead): print(f"{r}: {len(dead[r])}: {' '.join(sorted(dead[r]))[:300]}")
EOF

=== sig_said
A FILE'S SIGNATURE DIAGNOSTICS ARE ONE ANSWER: `sig_said` says what the signature rounds said, over files with and without refusals. No source in this corpus makes a signing round speak (every refusal tried is spoken by a later pass), so the equalities below pin the shape of the answer, not a message. 

=== settle_bill
A settlement is billed for what ITS OWN run holds. `type_named` asks the workspace, which builds types and signatures to answer and keeps them — memory the compiler made on the run's behalf, never the run's. A budget that counted it made a derive's fate depend on how much the compiler had already loaded: the same derive settled in 2 MB or was cut off past 5 MiB, and the cut dropped its declarations without a word. 

=== unit_reads
A unit is lowered once and reused by every compile-time run that reaches it, so a const its lowering reads is a read of EVERY run that uses it — never only of the run that lowered it first. 

=== reentry_run
A RE-ENTRY'S MEMORY BELONGS TO ITS OUTER RUN: what a file's first re-entrant expansion settled is read while that run is open, and a later revision's run starts with none of it. 

=== main_bucket
A FILE'S `main` IS ITS OWN. Every file with top-level statements mints a declaration named `main`, so the name's bucket holds one per file; a read of one file's `main` must depend on that file's rows, never on every other file's `main` — or a file gained anywhere in the program would move every entry's answer.

//! A TYPING TABLE CROSSES BY ITS CODEC, held by machine: a table read back is the table
//! written, field by field (the registry's `same_facts`), and a read the scope cannot place is
//! refused.
use compiler.{facts_exemplars, same_facts}
use core.{TypeId, side_table_of, expr_window}
use features.{TypeFacts}
use diagnostics.{Voices, Diag, error_at}
use @std.relation.stable.{Scope, CodecFault, indexed_scope}

/// The table with every column holding something.
fn sample() -> TypeFacts { facts_exemplars()[1] }

fn back(facts: TypeFacts) -> Result<TypeFacts, CodecFault> {
    TypeFacts.decoded_in(indexed_scope(), facts.encoded_in(indexed_scope()))
}

/// A scope whose inverse holds nothing: the wire it wrote names ids it can no longer resolve.
type Forgetful = {}

impl Scope for Forgetful {
    fn spelled(kind: string, index: int) -> string { "${index}" }

    fn unspelled(kind: string, text: string) -> int? { null }

    fn placed(file: string, lo: int, hi: int) -> List<int>? { null }

    fn unplaced(file: string, at: List<int>) -> List<int>? { null }
}

fn no_captures() -> List<List<TypeId>?> { [null] }

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""delfn.py FILE NAME... — delete top-level items (fn/type/const/enum/trait/impl X) named NAME, with
their leading /// docs and @annotations. Prints each item's line count; exits 1 if a name is not found."""
import re, sys
path, names = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
L = open(path).read().split('\n')
head = re.compile(r'^(?:export\s+)?(?:static\s+)?(?:once\s+)?(?:fn|type|const|enum|trait|struct|flag|option|collect)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)')
def strip_str(t):
    out=[]; q=False; esc=False
    for ch in t:
        if q:
            if esc: esc=False
            elif ch=='\\': esc=True
            elif ch=='"': q=False
            continue
        if ch=='"': q=True; continue
        if ch=='/' and out and out[-1]=='/': out.pop(); break
        out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)
def span(i):
    s = strip_str(L[i]); depth = s.count('{') + s.count('(') + s.count('[') - s.count('}') - s.count(')') - s.count(']')
    j = i
    angle = s.rstrip().endswith('<')
    while depth > 0 or angle or (j == i and s.rstrip().endswith(('{', '(', '[', '=', ','))):
        j += 1; t = strip_str(L[j])
        depth += t.count('{') + t.count('(') + t.count('[') - t.count('}') - t.count(')') - t.count(']')
        if t.startswith('>'): angle = False
        if depth <= 0 and not angle and (t[:1] in '})]>'): break
    b = i
    while b > 0 and (L[b-1].startswith('//') or L[b-1].startswith('@')): b -= 1
```

"""delmeth.py FILE NAME... — delete methods `    fn NAME` (4-space indent, inside impl blocks) with their
leading `    ///` docs and `    @` annotations. Prints the count deleted."""
import re, sys
path, names = sys.argv[1], set(sys.argv[2:])
L = open(path).read().split('\n'); out = []; i = 0; n = 0
head = re.compile(r'^    (?:export\s+)?(?:mut\s+|static\s+)*fn\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)')
while i < len(L):
    m = head.match(L[i])
    if m and m.group(1) in names:
        # drop the docs/annotations already emitted
        while out and (out[-1].startswith('    ///') or out[-1].startswith('    @')): out.pop()
        j = i
        if not L[i].rstrip().endswith('}') or L[i].count('{') != L[i].count('}'):
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(L) and not L[j].startswith('    }') : j += 1
        i = j + 1; n += 1
        if out and out[-1].strip() == '' and i < len(L) and L[i].strip() == '': i += 1
        continue
    out.append(L[i]); i += 1
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(out)); print(n)
EOF

/// EVERY NAME ONCE, SUMMED — the one grouping every `--time` report
/// wants: a coarse phase pushed once reads unchanged, a per-file span
/// pushed hundreds of times folds to its total instead of flooding
/// the line with one entry per file.
export fn grouped_phases(phases: List<Phase>) -> List<Phase> {
    [Phase {
        name: n,
        ns: phase_total(phases, n),
        mints: phase_sum([p.mints for p in phases if p.name == n]),
        settles: phase_sum([p.settles for p in phases if p.name == n]),
    } for n in distinct([p.name for p in phases])]
}

fn phase_sum(counts: List<int>) -> int { counts.fold(0, (sum, c) -> sum + c) }

export fn phase_total(phases: List<Phase>, name: string) -> int {
    mut total = 0
    for p in phases { if p.name == name { total = total + p.ns } }
    total
}

/// `Parsed`'s fingerprint over a `DbRow` value — the words a block
/// import brings in are folded so a dependency's grammar appearing
/// re-parses this file.

/// A PARSE'S OWN DIGEST — structural fingerprints and the block words it read, never a byte or
/// a comment. The family's cutoff and the record's `syntax` column are the same value, so a
/// file whose text moved but whose syntax did not is the same file to both.
export fn fingerprint_of_parsed(p: Parsed) -> int {
    fp(121, [program_hash(p), fp_str(joined(sorted_texts(p.store.sublang_words()), ","))])

/// path's own rule (`file_home`), or, belonging to none, a package of that one file — checked as the
/// old `check` says it, held to its baseline where one is named.
fn program_door_checked(args: CliResult, path: string) -> int {
    if is_a_dir(path) {
        let dir = rooted(path)
        if !exists_at(joined_path(dir, "avra.toml")) {
            println(render_among(no_manifest(dir, package_root(dir_of(dir))), []))
            return 1
        }
        if !is_a_dir(joined_path(dir, "src")) { return root_programs_checked(args, dir) }
    }
    let disk? = checked_disk(path) else { return std_unfound() }
    disk_checked(
        disk,
        args.option("baseline"),
        timed(args),
        args.has_flag("baseline_accept"),
        args.has_flag("counts"),
        args.has_flag("read_lists"),
    )
}

use answer_record.{ContentHash, RecordedRead, answer_record, content_hash, question}
use disk_store.{disk_store_at, frontier_file_path}
use frontier.{FrontierEntry, FrontierKind, base_file}
use sorted.{sorted_by}
use query_engine.{QueryDefinition, QueryEngine, query_engine}

/// What `name` answers about `argument`, asked as this binary asks it.
fn asked(e: QueryEngine, name: string, argument: string) -> string {
    e.answer_to(question(name, e.definitions.get().get(name)!.code_hash, argument.bytes())).copied().text() ?? ""
}

/// `text` reads the world; `length` counts a path's text; `parity` says whether that is even. Every
/// query's code is `code`.
fn binary(world: Map<string, string>, code: string) -> List<QueryDefinition> {
    let held = Cell.new(world)
    [
        QueryDefinition {
            query_name: "text",
            code_hash: code,
            is_input: true,
            compute: (_e, a) -> (held.get().get(a.text() ?? "") ?? "").bytes(),
        },
        QueryDefinition {
            query_name: "length",
            code_hash: code,
            is_input: false,
            compute: (e, a) -> "${asked(e, "text", a.text() ?? "").length}".bytes(),
        },
        QueryDefinition { query_name: "parity", code_hash: code, is_input: false, compute: parity_of },
    ]
}

fn parity_of(e: QueryEngine, a: Bytes) -> Bytes {
    let n = parse_int(asked(e, "length", a.text() ?? "")) ?? 0
    if n % 2 == 0 { "even" } else { "odd" }.bytes()
}

fn world_of(a: string) -> Map<string, string> {
    let w: Map<string, string> = {"a": a}
    w
}

fn fresh(label: string) -> string { "/tmp/avra-stored-cycles/${stamp()}-${label}" }

/// One whole process of `binary` over the store at `directory`: asks `name` of `a`, leaves its
/// frontier, publishes, and answers.
fn ran(directory: string, binary: List<QueryDefinition>, name: string) -> string {
    let store = disk_store_at(directory)
    let engine = query_engine(store, binary)
    let answer = asked(engine, name, "a")
    engine.frontier_kept()
    let _ = store.saved()
    answer
}

fn known_as(name: string, code: string) -> ContentHash { question(name, code, "a".bytes()).known_as }

/// Two kept records that read each other — `length` of `a` reading `parity` of `a`, and `parity`
/// reading `length` — each seeing an answer nothing holds, kept in `directory` and published.
fn records_read_each_other(directory: string) {
    let store = disk_store_at(directory)
    let _ = query_engine(store, binary(world_of("abc"), "c1"))
    let seen = content_hash("seen".bytes())
    let length = question("length", "c1", "a".bytes())
    let parity = question("parity", "c1", "a".bytes())
    store.keep_record(length, answer_record(content_hash("7".bytes()), [RecordedRead { question: parity.known_as, whole_answer: seen, part: null }]))
    store.keep_record(parity, answer_record(content_hash("even".bytes()), [RecordedRead { question: length.known_as, whole_answer: seen, part: null }]))
    let _ = store.saved()
}

/// A frontier for the binary of `code` in `directory` whose reads close a cycle: `length` reads
/// `parity`, `parity` reads `length`, and both read the input `text`, each answer one nothing holds.
fn cyclic_frontier(directory: string, code: string) {
    let _ = make_dirs(directory) catch ""
    let text = known_as("text", code)
    let length = known_as("length", code)
    let parity = known_as("parity", code)
    let order = sorted_by([text, length, parity], (x, y) -> x.comes_before(y))
    let at = (q: ContentHash) -> [i for i, o in order if o.same_as(q)].first() ?? 0
    let reads_of = (q: ContentHash) -> if q.same_as(length) { [at(parity), at(text)] } else if q.same_as(parity) { [at(length), at(text)] } else { [] }
    let entries = [FrontierEntry {
        question: q,
        answer: content_hash("nothing holds this".bytes()),
        reads: reads_of(q),
        input: q.same_as(text),
        root: !q.same_as(text),
    } for q in order]
    let base = base_file(entries, [], 1)
    let print = query_engine(disk_store_at("/dev/null/none"), binary(world_of(""), code)).print()
    let _ = write_bytes(frontier_file_path(directory, print, FrontierKind.Base, base.id), base.runs.bytes())
}

spec "a store's cycles end" {
    given "kept records that read each other" {
        then "a fresh process asks over them and answers what the world holds" {
            let directory = fresh("records")
            records_read_each_other(directory)
            ran(directory, binary(world_of("abc"), "c1"), "parity") == "odd"
        }
    }
    given "a frontier whose reads close a cycle, the world moved under it" {
        then "the process walks it, ends, and answers what the world holds" {
            let directory = fresh("frontier")
            cyclic_frontier(directory, "c1")
            ran(directory, binary(world_of("abcd"), "c1"), "parity") == "even"
        }
        then "and the next process, over what that one left, answers the same" {
            let directory = fresh("frontier-again")
            cyclic_frontier(directory, "c1")
            let _ = ran(directory, binary(world_of("abcd"), "c1"), "parity")
            ran(directory, binary(world_of("abcde"), "c1"), "parity") == "odd"
        }
    }
    given "a cyclic frontier another binary left" {
        then "it is never read: the process answers what the world holds" {
            let directory = fresh("foreign")
            cyclic_frontier(directory, "c2")
            ran(directory, binary(world_of("abc"), "c1"), "parity") == "odd"
        }
    }
}

lane spec-harness: **defect 2 (P0), both faults fixed by construction.** Commit **cbeb39ab** on branch `store-p0` (off group3-base 48cbe855, std-program only, 3 files).

- **Fault 1, the frontier walk.**
  - The walk wasn't endless in the strict sense: `reached_above` already had a seen-set and ran iteratively.
  - The cost was. `lost_from` ran `holders_of` per popped place, which ran a full `reached_above` per reader, recounting as readers joined the lost.
  - Over a frontier read back after a big change (the 25,000-line deletion), with stale readers, the work grows about as n^3.5. Measured: 160 places took 5 s, 400 took 127 s, and 600 was still running at 300 s.
  - **Fix:** the walk now spends from one budget, `WALK_PER_PLACE` (4) × extent + cut. Once that's spent it takes the whole walk from the roots (`reached_from_roots`: iterative, seen-set, linear). That walk finds exactly the same places (the `whole_walk_held` self-check already asserts the equality), so the frontier write is linear in the frontier's size whatever it holds, cycles included. `readers_of` is untouched.
- **Fault 2, the standing check's recursion.**
  - Verifying a kept record asks its reads again (`settled_by_asking → settled_answer → standing_answer → stands_now → …`), and they verify their own records. Nothing guarded a question that was already being verified, so records that read each other recursed until the stack overflowed.
  - **Fix:** the engine keeps a `verifying` set. A question asked again while it's being asked again can't vouch for itself, so the read doesn't hold, the record doesn't stand, and the answer is computed fresh.
  - That bounds the recursion by the number of distinct questions, so a record cycle can no longer overflow the stack. It isn't fully iterative: a legitimate dependency chain is still walked recursively. Making the engine's verification iterative is a larger engine change, and I'd want your go-ahead first.
- **Foreign prints:** already never read. `frontier_of(print)` and the pack listing take only files with the exact print (`answers_print`). The hang was over *this binary's own* frontier, after a huge change between trees.

  - a cyclic frontier, the next process over what it left, and a cyclic frontier under a foreign print: green before and after;
